ko.title: [Retailing 101 #9] 모든 통로는 작은 사업이고, 그것의 고유한 P&L이 있습니다

segments.src: > One-line summary: Advanced merchandising means running each category like a standalone business — giving it a job to do, measuring the return on the cash parked in its inventory, and setting prices that protect both margin and price image.
segments.tr: > 한 줄 요약: 고급 상품 배치란 각 카테고리를 독립적인 사업처럼 운영하는 것 — 그것에 역할을 부여하고, 재고에 묶여 있는 현금이 벌어들인 수익을 측정하고, 마진과 가격 이미지 모두를 지키는 가격을 책정하는 것입니다.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: Last time we met the person who picked everything on the shelf six months before you walked in.
segments.tr: 지난번에 우리는 당신이 들어오기 6개월 전에 선반의 모든 상품을 선택한 사람을 만났습니다.

segments.src: Today: how they actually decide.
segments.tr: 오늘은: 그들이 실제로 어떻게 결정하는지.

segments.src: Three levers do most of the work.
segments.tr: 세 가지 레버가 대부분의 업무를 수행합니다.

segments.src: Category management — the aisle has a job.**
segments.tr: 카테고리 관리 — 이 통로가 해야 할 역할이 있습니다.**

segments.src: Instead of buying product by product, retailers group items the way shoppers think about them ("oral care," not "tubes we get from Colgate") and manage that group as a business unit.
segments.tr: 소매점들은 제품 하나하나를 사기보다는 쇼핑객들이 생각하는 방식대로 상품을 그룹화하고("콜게이트에서 받는 튜브들"이 아니라 "구강 관리") 그 그룹을 사업 단위로 관리합니다.

segments.src: The framework, popularized in the 1990s through the industry's Efficient Consumer Response push, starts by assigning each category a **role**:
segments.tr: 1990년대에 업계의 효율적 소비자 대응(Efficient Consumer Response) 추진을 통해 대중화된 이 프레임워크는 각 카테고리에 **역할**을 할당하는 것으로 시작합니다:

segments.src: - **Destination** — a reason to choose this store over the one down the road. Deep assortment, sharp prices, lots of space.
segments.tr: - **목적지** — 이 가게를 길 아래 다른 가게 대신 선택할 이유. 다양한 상품 구성, 경쟁력 있는 가격, 넓은 매장 공간.

segments.src: - **Routine** — the everyday workhorse that builds the basket and carries margin. Most of the store lives here.
segments.tr: - **루틴** — 장바구니를 채우고 마진을 가져오는 일상의 주역. 대부분의 매장이 여기 있습니다.

segments.src: - **Occasional / seasonal** — grilling supplies in June, school glue in August.
segments.tr: - **불규칙·계절** — 6월의 그릴 용품, 8월의 학용 접착제.

segments.src: - **Convenience** — you didn't come for it, but it's there. Fewer options, healthier margins.
segments.tr: - **편의** — 당신이 이것을 위해 온 것은 아니지만, 그것은 여기 있습니다. 적은 선택지, 더 높은 마진.

segments.src: The role drives everything downstream: how many SKUs, how much shelf, how aggressive the price, how much promo money.
segments.tr: 역할은 모든 하위 항목을 주도합니다: SKU 개수, 선반 공간, 가격 공격성, 프로모션 금액.

segments.src: A destination category and a convenience category get opposite treatment on purpose.
segments.tr: 목적지 카테고리와 편의 카테고리는 의도적으로 반대 대우를 받습니다.

segments.src: One wrinkle worth knowing: retailers often name a **category captain** — usually the biggest supplier — to help build the plan, since that vendor has the best data.
segments.tr: 알아두면 좋은 주름: 소매점들은 종종 계획을 세우는 것을 도와줄 **카테고리 캡틴**(보통 가장 큰 공급자)을 지정합니다. 그 공급자가 최고의 데이터를 가지고 있기 때문입니다.

segments.src: It's efficient and it's a conflict of interest at the same time, which is why captains' recommendations get audited and why the practice draws antitrust attention.
segments.tr: 그것은 효율적이면서 동시에 이해 충돌이고, 이것이 캡틴의 권고가 감시받고 이 관행이 반독점 주의를 끌 수 있는 이유입니다.

segments.src: Inventory management — the shelf is a bank account.**
segments.tr: 재고 관리 — 선반은 은행 계좌입니다.**

segments.src: Every unit on that shelf is cash the retailer can't use for anything else.
segments.tr: 선반 위의 모든 단위는 소매점이 다른 용도로 사용할 수 없는 현금입니다.

segments.src: So the question isn't "did it sell?"
segments.tr: 그래서 문제는 "팔렸는가?"가 아니라

segments.src: but "what did it earn per dollar tied up?"
segments.tr: "묶여 있는 달러당 얼마를 벌었는가?"입니다.

segments.src: Two numbers carry the load:
segments.tr: 두 가지 숫자가 핵심입니다:

segments.src: inventory turnover = cost of goods sold / average inventory at cost
segments.tr: inventory turnover = cost of goods sold / average inventory at cost

segments.src: GMROI = gross margin dollars / average inventory at cost
segments.tr: GMROI = gross margin dollars / average inventory at cost

segments.src: weeks of supply = 52 / annual turns
segments.tr: weeks of supply = 52 / annual turns

segments.src: GMROI of 2.5 means the category returned $2.50 of gross margin for every $1 invested in inventory.
segments.tr: GMROI가 2.5라는 것은 그 카테고리가 재고에 투자된 $1마다 $2.50의 총 마진을 반환했다는 뜻입니다.

segments.src: This is why a low-margin item that turns 20 times a year can beat a high-margin item that turns twice — and why buyers argue about turns more than about markup.
segments.tr: 이것이 저마진 상품이 연간 20회 회전해서 2회 회전하는 고마진 상품을 이길 수 있는 이유이고, 구매자들이 마진보다 회전수에 대해 더 많이 논쟁하는 이유입니다.

segments.src: The counterweight is service level.
segments.tr: 균형을 맞추는 것은 서비스 수준입니다.

segments.src: Order less and you free cash but risk an out-of-stock, which costs the sale and sometimes the trip.
segments.tr: 적게 주문하면 현금은 확보하지만 품절 위험이 있고, 이는 판매와 때로는 쇼핑 여행 자체를 잃을 수 있습니다.

segments.src: So teams hold **safety stock** and set a reorder point:
segments.tr: 그래서 팀들은 **안전 재고**를 유지하고 재주문 시점을 설정합니다:

segments.src: reorder point = expected demand during lead time + safety stock
segments.tr: reorder point = expected demand during lead time + safety stock

segments.src: Then there's leakage.
segments.tr: 그 다음은 손실입니다.

segments.src: **Shrink** — theft, damage, spoilage, paperwork errors — has run around 1.5% of sales in recent National Retail Federation security surveys.
segments.tr: **감손** — 절도, 손상, 부패, 서류 오류 — 최근 전국 소매 연맹의 보안 조사에서 판매액의 약 1.5%를 차지했습니다.

segments.src: On thin retail margins, that's not rounding.
segments.tr: 소매 마진이 얇을 때 그것은 무시할 수 없는 숫자입니다.

segments.src: Pricing — margin and image, at the same time.**
segments.tr: 가격 책정 — 마진과 이미지, 동시에.**

segments.src: The arithmetic is easy:
segments.tr: 산술은 쉽습니다:

segments.src: retail price = cost / (1 - target margin %)
segments.tr: retail price = cost / (1 - target margin %)

segments.src: "Keystone" markup just means doubling cost: a $5 item retails at $10, a 50% margin.
segments.tr: "Keystone" 마크업은 단순히 원가를 두 배로 하는 것입니다: $5 아이템이 $10으로 소매되고, 50% 마진입니다.

segments.src: The strategy is the hard part, and it splits two ways.
segments.tr: 전략이 어려운 부분이고, 두 가지 방식으로 나뉩니다.

segments.src: **EDLP** (everyday low price) keeps prices flat and predictable — Walmart, Costco, Aldi.
segments.tr: **EDLP**(매일 낮은 가격)는 가격을 평평하고 예측 가능하게 유지합니다 — Walmart, Costco, Aldi.

segments.src: **High–low** runs a base price plus frequent, deep promotions, often gated behind a loyalty card — most conventional supermarkets and department stores.
segments.tr: **High–low**는 기본 가격에 빈번한 깊은 프로모션을 더하며, 종종 로열티 카드로 제한됩니다 — 대부분의 기존 슈퍼마켓과 백화점들.

segments.src: EDLP smooths demand and cuts labor spent re-ticketing; high–low creates urgency and pulls in deal-sensitive shoppers, at the cost of training people to wait for the sale.
segments.tr: EDLP는 수요를 평탄하게 하고 재표시에 소요되는 노동을 줄입니다; high–low는 긴박감을 만들고 거래에 민감한 쇼핑객을 끌어당기지만, 사람들을 세일을 기다리도록 훈련하는 비용이 발생합니다.

segments.src: Either way, no one prices 40,000 items with equal care.
segments.tr: 어느 쪽이든, 아무도 40,000개의 아이템을 동일하게 신경 써서 가격을 책정하지 않습니다.

segments.src: Shoppers only remember a few dozen **key value items** — milk, eggs, bananas, a 12-pack of soda — and those set the store's price image.
segments.tr: 쇼핑객들은 수십 개의 **핵심 가치 아이템**만 기억합니다 — 우유, 계란, 바나나, 12팩 소다 — 그리고 그것들이 매장의 가격 이미지를 결정합니다.

segments.src: Those get priced sharply, sometimes at or below cost as a **loss leader**, and the margin is recovered on the rest of the basket.
segments.tr: 그것들은 날카롭게 가격이 책정되며, 때로는 **손실 리더**로서 원가 또는 그 이하로 가격이 책정되고, 마진은 장바구니의 나머지 항목에서 회복됩니다.

segments.src: (Loss leaders are generally legal, though a number of states have minimum-markup laws, usually covering gas, alcohol, or tobacco.)
segments.tr: (손실 리더는 일반적으로 합법이지만, 많은 주들이 최소 마크업 법을 가지고 있으며, 보통 휘발유, 알코올 또는 담배를 다룹니다.)

segments.src: And when inventory ages, **markdowns** are the release valve: a planned cadence of cuts that converts stale stock back into cash before it's worth nothing.
segments.tr: 그리고 재고가 낡으면, **마크다운**은 배출 밸브입니다: 낡은 재고를 가치가 없기 전에 현금으로 변환하는 계획된 할인들입니다.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 일상생활에서

segments.src: Sunday morning, a Kroger on the north side of Columbus.
segments.tr: 일요일 아침, 콜럼버스 북쪽의 Kroger.

segments.src: Your cart: a gallon of milk, cereal, toothpaste, tortilla chips, a rotisserie chicken.
segments.tr: 당신의 카트: 우유 1갤론, 시리얼, 치약, 토르티야 칩, 로티세리 닭.

segments.src: The milk is a key value item.
segments.tr: 우유는 핵심 가치 아이템입니다.

segments.src: It's priced within pennies of the Meijer two miles away because management assumes you know roughly what milk costs.
segments.tr: 2마일 떨어진 Meijer의 우유와 거의 같은 가격으로 책정되어 있습니다. 경영진이 당신이 대략 우유가 얼마나 비싼지 안다고 가정하기 때문입니다.

segments.src: The rotisserie chicken is close to a loss leader — cooked from a bird that would've been marked down anyway, priced to get you through the door on the one trip where you might also buy a $30 cut of steak.
segments.tr: 로티세리 닭은 손실 리더에 가깝습니다 — 어차피 마크다운될 새에서 요리되었고, 당신이 $30 스테이크를 사거나 할 수 있는 한 번의 여행에서 문을 통해 들어가게 하기 위해 가격이 책정되었습니다.

segments.src: Costco has famously held its chicken at $4.99 for years for exactly this reason.
segments.tr: Costco는 정확히 이 이유로 몇 년 동안 닭을 $4.99에 유지해왔습니다.

segments.src: The toothpaste tells the category story.
segments.tr: 치약은 카테고리 이야기를 말해줍니다.

segments.src: Oral care is a routine category here, so you get maybe 40 SKUs, not 90, and the shelf runs a familiar pattern: a national brand at eye level, the Kroger store brand right beside it at a lower price and a higher margin, and the $9 whitening kit on the top shelf where it turns slowly but earns well when it does.
segments.tr: 구강 관리는 여기서 루틴 카테고리이므로, 90개가 아니라 40개 정도의 SKU를 얻게 되며, 선반은 친숙한 패턴을 따릅니다: 눈높이에 있는 전국 브랜드, Kroger 자체 브랜드가 바로 옆에 더 낮은 가격과 더 높은 마진으로, 그리고 $9 미백 키트가 위쪽 선반에 있어서 천천히 회전하지만 할 때 잘 벌어들입니다.

segments.src: The chips are near the front — high turns, decent margin, impulse-friendly placement.
segments.tr: 칩은 앞쪽 근처에 있습니다 — 높은 회전율, 괜찮은 마진, 충동구매 친화적 배치.

segments.src: And the endcap you walked past with the seasonal cooler display?
segments.tr: 그리고 당신이 지나간, 계절 냉음료 디스플레이가 있는 끝 매대?

segments.src: That's an occasional category, bought in a single seasonal buy, with a markdown schedule already written for late August.
segments.tr: 그것은 불규칙 카테고리이고, 한 번의 계절 구매에서 구매되며, 8월 말을 위한 마크다운 일정이 이미 작성되어 있습니다.

segments.src: Nobody will scramble when it stops selling.
segments.tr: 그것이 팔리지 않을 때 아무도 서두르지 않을 것입니다.

segments.src: That was the plan in April.
segments.tr: 그것이 4월의 계획이었습니다.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 세 줄 요약

segments.src: 1. Category management treats each group of products as a business with an assigned role — destination, routine, occasional, or convenience — and that role drives assortment, space, and price aggressiveness.
segments.tr: 1. 카테고리 관리는 각 상품 그룹을 할당된 역할(목적지, 루틴, 불규칙, 편의)이 있는 사업으로 취급하며, 그 역할은 상품 구성, 공간, 가격 공격성을 주도합니다.

segments.src: 2. Inventory is capital, so retailers judge it by turns and GMROI (gross margin per dollar invested), balancing that against the cost of being out of stock.
segments.tr: 2. 재고는 자본이므로 소매점들은 회전율과 GMROI(투자된 달러당 총 마진)로 판단하며, 그것을 품절 비용과 균형을 맞춥니다.

segments.src: 3. Pricing is a portfolio: sharp on the handful of key value items that shape price image, and recovered across everything else — under either an EDLP or a high–low strategy.
segments.tr: 3. 가격 책정은 포트폴리오입니다: 가격 이미지를 형성하는 소수의 핵심 가치 아이템들에서는 날카롭게, 그 외 모든 것에서 회복됩니다 — EDLP 또는 high–low 전략 중 하나에서.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 자가진단 퀴즈

segments.src: **1.** A category posts a GMROI of 3.0.
segments.tr: **1.** 한 카테고리가 GMROI 3.0을 기록합니다.

segments.src: What does that mean?
segments.tr: 그것이 무엇을 의미합니까?

segments.src: A) It sold three times more than last year
segments.tr: A) 작년보다 3배 더 많이 팔렸습니다

segments.src: B) It earned $3.00 of gross margin per $1 invested in inventory at cost
segments.tr: B) 원가로 계산한 재고에 투자된 $1당 $3.00의 총 마진을 벌었습니다

segments.src: C) Its gross margin is 30%
segments.tr: C) 총 마진율은 30%입니다

segments.src: D) It turns three times per week
segments.tr: D) 주당 3회 회전합니다

segments.src: **2.** O / X — An EDLP retailer's core strategy is running deep weekly promotions to create urgency.
segments.tr: **2.** O / X — EDLP 소매점의 핵심 전략은 긴박감을 만들기 위해 깊은 주간 프로모션을 운영하는 것입니다.

segments.src: **3.** In a supermarket, "milk and eggs, priced to match the competitor down the street" is best described as:
segments.tr: **3.** 슈퍼마켓에서 "거리 아래 경쟁사와 맞추는 가격의 우유와 계란"은 가장 잘 설명되는 것입니다:

segments.src: A) A convenience category
segments.tr: A) 편의 카테고리

segments.src: B) A seasonal buy
segments.tr: B) 계절 구매

segments.src: C) Key value items in a destination/traffic-driving role
segments.tr: C) 목적지/트래픽 주도 역할의 핵심 가치 아이템들

segments.src: D) A markdown cadence
segments.tr: D) 마크다운 주기

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **Category management** — Managing a group of related products as a single business unit with its own role, strategy, and scorecard, rather than item by item.
segments.tr: - **카테고리 관리** — 제품 하나하나가 아니라 자신의 역할, 전략, 성과표를 가진 단일 사업 단위로서 관련된 상품 그룹을 관리하는 것.

segments.src: - **Category role** — The job assigned to a category (destination, routine, occasional/seasonal, convenience), which determines its space, assortment breadth, and pricing posture.
segments.tr: - **카테고리 역할** — 카테고리에 할당된 역할(목적지, 루틴, 불규칙·계절, 편의)은 그 공간, 상품 구성 폭, 가격 책정 자세를 결정합니다.

segments.src: - **GMROI** — Gross margin return on inventory investment: gross margin dollars divided by average inventory at cost; the profit earned per dollar tied up in stock.
segments.tr: - **GMROI** — 재고 투자에 대한 총 마진 반환: 총 마진 달러를 원가 평균 재고로 나눔; 재고에 묶인 달러당 벌어들인 이익.

segments.src: - **Inventory turnover** — How many times a year inventory is sold and replaced (COGS ÷ average inventory at cost); higher turns free up cash and reduce markdown risk.
segments.tr: - **재고 회전율** — 연간 재고가 판매되고 교체되는 횟수(COGS ÷ 원가 평균 재고); 더 높은 회전율은 현금을 확보하고 마크다운 위험을 줄입니다.

segments.src: - **EDLP vs. high–low** — Two pricing strategies: consistently low everyday prices, versus a higher base price punctuated by frequent deep promotions.
segments.tr: - **EDLP vs. high–low** — 두 가지 가격 책정 전략: 지속적으로 낮은 일일 가격 vs. 빈번한 깊은 프로모션으로 구분되는 더 높은 기본 가격.

segments.src: *Answers: 1 — B.
GMROI is gross margin dollars ÷ average inventory at cost, so 3.0 means $3.00 of gross margin per $1 of inventory investment.

segments.src: It says nothing directly about margin percentage or growth.
segments.tr: 마진 비율이나 성장에 대해 직접적으로 아무것도 말하지 않습니다.

segments.src: 2 — X (False).
That describes high–low pricing; EDLP deliberately avoids the promo cycle in favor of stable, predictable prices.

segments.src: Milk and eggs are classic key value items whose prices shoppers actually remember, so they're priced to build traffic and price image, with margin recovered elsewhere in the basket.*

zh.title: [零售101 #9] 每条走廊都是一个小企业，拥有自己的损益表

segments.src: > One-line summary: Advanced merchandising means running each category like a standalone business — giving it a job to do, measuring the return on the cash parked in its inventory, and setting prices that protect both margin and price image.
segments.tr: > 单行总结：先进的商品陈列意味着像运营独立业务一样运营每个商品类别——给它分配一个任务，衡量其库存资金的回报，制定既能保护利润率又能维护品牌形象的价格。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今天的概念

segments.src: Last time we met the person who picked everything on the shelf six months before you walked in.
segments.tr: 上次我们见到了在你走进来的六个月前选择架子上所有商品的那个人。

segments.src: Today: how they actually decide.
segments.tr: 今天：他们是如何真正做出决定的。

segments.src: Three levers do most of the work.
segments.tr: 三个杠杆做了大部分工作。

segments.src: Category management — the aisle has a job.**
segments.tr: 商品类别管理——走廊有一个任务。**

segments.src: Instead of buying product by product, retailers group items the way shoppers think about them ("oral care," not "tubes we get from Colgate") and manage that group as a business unit.
segments.tr: 零售商不是逐件购买产品，而是按照购物者的思维方式分组（"口腔护理"，而不是"我们从高露洁买的管子"），并将这个群体作为一个业务单位来管理。

segments.src: The framework, popularized in the 1990s through the industry's Efficient Consumer Response push, starts by assigning each category a **role**:
segments.tr: 这个框架在20世纪90年代通过该行业的有效消费者反应推动而流行，首先为每个商品类别分配一个**角色**：

segments.src: - **Destination** — a reason to choose this store over the one down the road. Deep assortment, sharp prices, lots of space.
segments.tr: - **目的地** ——选择这家店而不是街道对面那一家的理由。深层次的商品范围、优惠价格、大量空间。

segments.src: - **Routine** — the everyday workhorse that builds the basket and carries margin. Most of the store lives here.
segments.tr: - **日常** ——日常的主力产品，支撑篮子并产生利润。大部分商店都在这里。

segments.src: - **Occasional / seasonal** — grilling supplies in June, school glue in August.
segments.tr: - **偶发/季节性** ——6月的烧烤用品，8月的学用胶水。

segments.src: - **Convenience** — you didn't come for it, but it's there. Fewer options, healthier margins.
segments.tr: - **便利** ——你不是为它来的，但它就在那里。选项较少，利润率更高。

segments.src: The role drives everything downstream: how many SKUs, how much shelf, how aggressive the price, how much promo money.
segments.tr: 这个角色会影响下游的一切：有多少SKU、多少货架空间、价格有多激进、有多少促销资金。

segments.src: A destination category and a convenience category get opposite treatment on purpose.
segments.tr: 目的地商品类别和便利商品类别有意受到相反的对待。

segments.src: One wrinkle worth knowing: retailers often name a **category captain** — usually the biggest supplier — to help build the plan, since that vendor has the best data.
segments.tr: 一个值得了解的细节：零售商通常会指定一个**商品类别负责人**——通常是最大的供应商——帮助制定计划，因为那个供应商拥有最好的数据。

segments.src: It's efficient and it's a conflict of interest at the same time, which is why captains' recommendations get audited and why the practice draws antitrust attention.
segments.tr: 这既高效又存在利益冲突，这就是为什么负责人的建议会受到审查，以及为什么这种做法会引起反垄断关注。

segments.src: Inventory management — the shelf is a bank account.**
segments.tr: 库存管理——货架是一个银行账户。**

segments.src: Every unit on that shelf is cash the retailer can't use for anything else.
segments.tr: 架子上的每一件商品都是零售商无法用于其他任何事情的现金。

segments.src: So the question isn't "did it sell?"
segments.tr: 所以问题不是"它卖出去了吗？"

segments.src: but "what did it earn per dollar tied up?"
segments.tr: 而是"它每投资一美元能赚多少？"

segments.src: Two numbers carry the load:
segments.tr: 两个数字承担了重任：

segments.src: inventory turnover = cost of goods sold / average inventory at cost
segments.tr: inventory turnover = cost of goods sold / average inventory at cost

segments.src: GMROI = gross margin dollars / average inventory at cost
segments.tr: GMROI = gross margin dollars / average inventory at cost

segments.src: weeks of supply = 52 / annual turns
segments.tr: weeks of supply = 52 / annual turns

segments.src: GMROI of 2.5 means the category returned $2.50 of gross margin for every $1 invested in inventory.
segments.tr: 2.5的GMROI意味着该商品类别对投资于库存的每1美元返回了2.50美元的毛利。

segments.src: This is why a low-margin item that turns 20 times a year can beat a high-margin item that turns twice — and why buyers argue about turns more than about markup.
segments.tr: 这就是为什么年转速20倍的低利润率商品可能会击败年转速2次的高利润率商品——以及为什么买家们争论转速比争论标价更多的原因。

segments.src: The counterweight is service level.
segments.tr: 抗衡力是服务水平。

segments.src: Order less and you free cash but risk an out-of-stock, which costs the sale and sometimes the trip.
segments.tr: 订单减少可以释放现金，但冒着缺货风险，这会让销售和有时甚至整趟购物无法成交。

segments.src: So teams hold **safety stock** and set a reorder point:
segments.tr: 所以团队持有**安全库存**并设置再订购点：

segments.src: reorder point = expected demand during lead time + safety stock
segments.tr: reorder point = expected demand during lead time + safety stock

segments.src: Then there's leakage.
segments.tr: 然后是损耗。

segments.src: **Shrink** — theft, damage, spoilage, paperwork errors — has run around 1.5% of sales in recent National Retail Federation security surveys.
segments.tr: **缩水** ——盗窃、损坏、变质、文书错误——在最近的全国零售联合会安全调查中约占销售额的1.5%。

segments.src: On thin retail margins, that's not rounding.
segments.tr: 在零售利润率微薄的情况下，这不是舍入误差。

segments.src: Pricing — margin and image, at the same time.**
segments.tr: 价格——利润率和形象，同时兼顾。**

segments.src: The arithmetic is easy:
segments.tr: 算术很简单：

segments.src: retail price = cost / (1 - target margin %)
segments.tr: retail price = cost / (1 - target margin %)

segments.src: "Keystone" markup just means doubling cost: a $5 item retails at $10, a 50% margin.
segments.tr: "Keystone"标价只是成本的两倍：一件5美元的商品零售价为10美元，50%的利润率。

segments.src: The strategy is the hard part, and it splits two ways.
segments.tr: 策略是难的部分，它分为两种方式。

segments.src: **EDLP** (everyday low price) keeps prices flat and predictable — Walmart, Costco, Aldi.
segments.tr: **EDLP**（每日低价）保持价格平稳且可预测——沃尔玛、好市多、Aldi。

segments.src: **High–low** runs a base price plus frequent, deep promotions, often gated behind a loyalty card — most conventional supermarkets and department stores.
segments.tr: **高低价**运行基础价格加上频繁的深度促销，通常被锁定在忠诚度卡后面——大多数传统超市和百货商店。

segments.src: EDLP smooths demand and cuts labor spent re-ticketing; high–low creates urgency and pulls in deal-sensitive shoppers, at the cost of training people to wait for the sale.
segments.tr: EDLP平滑需求并减少花费在重新贴标签上的劳动力；高低价创造紧迫感并吸引对交易敏感的购物者，代价是培养人们等待销售的习惯。

segments.src: Either way, no one prices 40,000 items with equal care.
segments.tr: 无论哪种方式，没有人以同等的谨慎态度为40,000件商品定价。

segments.src: Shoppers only remember a few dozen **key value items** — milk, eggs, bananas, a 12-pack of soda — and those set the store's price image.
segments.tr: 购物者只记得几十个**关键价值商品** ——牛奶、鸡蛋、香蕉、一包12罐汽水——这些设定了商店的价格形象。

segments.src: Those get priced sharply, sometimes at or below cost as a **loss leader**, and the margin is recovered on the rest of the basket.
segments.tr: 这些商品的价格被设置得很低，有时甚至低于成本充当**亏本商品**，利润则从篮子中的其他商品上弥补。

segments.src: (Loss leaders are generally legal, though a number of states have minimum-markup laws, usually covering gas, alcohol, or tobacco.)
segments.tr: （亏本商品通常是合法的，尽管许多州有最低标价法，通常涵盖汽油、酒精或烟草。）

segments.src: And when inventory ages, **markdowns** are the release valve: a planned cadence of cuts that converts stale stock back into cash before it's worth nothing.
segments.tr: 当库存老化时，**降价**是释放阀：一个计划好的削减节奏，在陈旧库存一文不值之前将其转换回现金。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活中

segments.src: Sunday morning, a Kroger on the north side of Columbus.
segments.tr: 星期天上午，哥伦布北部的一家Kroger。

segments.src: Your cart: a gallon of milk, cereal, toothpaste, tortilla chips, a rotisserie chicken.
segments.tr: 你的购物篮：一加仑牛奶、麦片、牙膏、玉米饼条、一只烤鸡。

segments.src: The milk is a key value item.
segments.tr: 牛奶是一个关键价值商品。

segments.src: It's priced within pennies of the Meijer two miles away because management assumes you know roughly what milk costs.
segments.tr: 它的价格在两英里外的Meijer的价格范围内波动几分钱，因为管理层假设你大概知道牛奶成本多少。

segments.src: The rotisserie chicken is close to a loss leader — cooked from a bird that would've been marked down anyway, priced to get you through the door on the one trip where you might also buy a $30 cut of steak.
segments.tr: 烤鸡接近于一个亏本商品——用本来会被降价处理的鸡烹饪而成，定价目的是让你在那一趟可能还会买一块30美元牛排的购物中走进门。

segments.src: Costco has famously held its chicken at $4.99 for years for exactly this reason.
segments.tr: Costco多年来一直以这个确切的原因将其鸡肉保持在4.99美元。

segments.src: The toothpaste tells the category story.
segments.tr: 牙膏讲述了商品类别的故事。

segments.src: Oral care is a routine category here, so you get maybe 40 SKUs, not 90, and the shelf runs a familiar pattern: a national brand at eye level, the Kroger store brand right beside it at a lower price and a higher margin, and the $9 whitening kit on the top shelf where it turns slowly but earns well when it does.
segments.tr: 口腔护理是这里的日常类别，所以你会得到大约40个SKU，而不是90个，货架呈现一个熟悉的模式：一个在眼睛水平的国家品牌，Kroger自有品牌紧靠它的左边以更低的价格和更高的利润率，还有排在最上面的9美元美白套装，它转速缓慢但当它转动时赚钱。

segments.src: The chips are near the front — high turns, decent margin, impulse-friendly placement.
segments.tr: 薯片靠近前面——高转速、不错的利润率、冲动友好的位置。

segments.src: And the endcap you walked past with the seasonal cooler display?
segments.tr: 你经过的端头展示，还有那个季节性冷却器展示？

segments.src: That's an occasional category, bought in a single seasonal buy, with a markdown schedule already written for late August.
segments.tr: 那是一个偶发商品类别，在单一的季节采购中购买，已经为8月底写好了降价计划。

segments.src: Nobody will scramble when it stops selling.
segments.tr: 当它停止销售时，没有人会争先恐后。

segments.src: That was the plan in April.
segments.tr: 那是4月的计划。

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 三行总结

segments.src: 1. Category management treats each group of products as a business with an assigned role — destination, routine, occasional, or convenience — and that role drives assortment, space, and price aggressiveness.
segments.tr: 1. 商品类别管理将每个产品组视为具有分配角色的业务——目的地、日常、偶发或便利——该角色驱动商品范围、空间和价格激进性。

segments.src: 2. Inventory is capital, so retailers judge it by turns and GMROI (gross margin per dollar invested), balancing that against the cost of being out of stock.
segments.tr: 2. 库存是资本，所以零售商通过转速和GMROI（投资美元的毛利）来判断它，并将其与缺货成本相平衡。

segments.src: 3. Pricing is a portfolio: sharp on the handful of key value items that shape price image, and recovered across everything else — under either an EDLP or a high–low strategy.
segments.tr: 3. 定价是一个组合：在塑造价格形象的少数关键价值商品上价格锐利，在所有其他商品上恢复——在EDLP或高低价策略下。

segments.src: ## ✅ Self Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 自我测验

segments.src: **1.** A category posts a GMROI of 3.0.
segments.tr: **1.** 一个商品类别发布了3.0的GMROI。

segments.src: What does that mean?
segments.tr: 这意味着什么？

segments.src: A) It sold three times more than last year
segments.tr: A) 与去年相比销售额增加了三倍

segments.src: B) It earned $3.00 of gross margin per $1 invested in inventory at cost
segments.tr: B) 它每投资成本1美元的库存赚取了3.00美元的毛利

segments.src: C) Its gross margin is 30%
segments.tr: C) 其毛利是30%

segments.src: D) It turns three times per week
segments.tr: D) 它每周转三次

segments.src: **2.** O / X — An EDLP retailer's core strategy is running deep weekly promotions to create urgency.
segments.tr: **2.** O / X —— EDLP零售商的核心策略是运行深度周促销以创造紧迫感。

segments.src: **3.** In a supermarket, "milk and eggs, priced to match the competitor down the street" is best described as:
segments.tr: **3.** 在超市中，"牛奶和鸡蛋，定价以匹配街道对面的竞争对手"最好描述为：

segments.src: A) A convenience category
segments.tr: A) 便利商品类别

segments.src: B) A seasonal buy
segments.tr: B) 季节性采购

segments.src: C) Key value items in a destination/traffic-driving role
segments.tr: C) 目的地/流量驱动角色中的关键价值商品

segments.src: D) A markdown cadence
segments.tr: D) 降价节奏

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 今天的术语

segments.src: - **Category management** — Managing a group of related products as a single business unit with its own role, strategy, and scorecard, rather than item by item.
segments.tr: - **商品类别管理** ——将一组相关产品作为单一业务单位进行管理，具有自己的角色、战略和计分卡，而不是逐件管理。

segments.src: - **Category role** — The job assigned to a category (destination, routine, occasional/seasonal, convenience), which determines its space, assortment breadth, and pricing posture.
segments.tr: - **商品类别角色** ——分配给商品类别的工作（目的地、日常、偶发/季节性、便利），它决定了其空间、商品范围广度和定价立场。

segments.src: - **GMROI** — Gross margin return on inventory investment: gross margin dollars divided by average inventory at cost; the profit earned per dollar tied up in stock.
segments.tr: - **GMROI** ——库存投资的毛利回报：毛利美元除以平均库存成本；库存中每投入美元赚取的利润。

segments.src: - **Inventory turnover** — How many times a year inventory is sold and replaced (COGS ÷ average inventory at cost); higher turns free up cash and reduce markdown risk.
segments.tr: - **库存周转** ——库存每年被销售和替换的次数（COGS÷平均库存成本）；更高的周转释放现金并降低降价风险。

segments.src: - **EDLP vs. high–low** — Two pricing strategies: consistently low everyday prices, versus a higher base price punctuated by frequent deep promotions.
segments.tr: - **EDLP与高低价** ——两种定价策略：持续的低廉每日价格，与频繁的深度促销相比较的更高基价。

segments.src: *Answers: 1 — B.
GMROI is gross margin dollars ÷ average inventory at cost, so 3.0 means $3.00 of gross margin per $1 of inventory investment.
segments.tr: GMROI是毛利美元÷平均库存成本，所以3.0意味着每投资1美元库存赚取3.00美元的毛利。

segments.src: It says nothing directly about margin percentage or growth.
segments.tr: 它对利润率百分比或增长没有直接说明。

segments.src: 2 — X (False).
That describes high–low pricing; EDLP deliberately avoids the promo cycle in favor of stable, predictable prices.
segments.tr: 这描述的是高低价定价；EDLP故意避免促销周期，转而采用稳定、可预测的价格。

segments.src: Milk and eggs are classic key value items whose prices shoppers actually remember, so they're priced to build traffic and price image, with margin recovered elsewhere in the basket.*
segments.tr: 牛奶和鸡蛋是购物者实际记住的经典关键价值商品，所以它们的定价是为了建立流量和价格形象，利润从篮子中的其他地方恢复。*

hi.title: [Retailing 101 #9] हर गलियारा एक छोटा व्यवसाय है, और इसका अपना P&L है

segments.src: > One-line summary: Advanced merchandising means running each category like a standalone business — giving it a job to do, measuring the return on the cash parked in its inventory, and setting prices that protect both margin and price image.
segments.tr: > एक पंक्ति का सारांश: उन्नत वस्तु प्रदर्शन का मतलब है प्रत्येक श्रेणी को एक स्वतंत्र व्यवसाय के रूप में चलाना — इसे एक काम देना, अपनी इन्वेंटरी में बंद नकद पर रिटर्न को मापना, और कीमतें निर्धारित करना जो मार्जिन और मूल्य छवि दोनों की रक्षा करते हैं।

segments.src: ## Today's Concept

segments.src: Last time we met the person who picked everything on the shelf six months before you walked in.
segments.tr: पिछली बार हम उस व्यक्ति से मिले जिसने छह महीने पहले आपके आने से पहले शेल्फ पर सब कुछ चुना था।

segments.src: Today: how they actually decide.
segments.tr: आज: वे वास्तव में कैसे निर्णय लेते हैं।

segments.src: Three levers do most of the work.
segments.tr: तीन लीवर अधिकांश काम करते हैं।

segments.src: Category management — the aisle has a job.**
segments.tr: श्रेणी प्रबंधन — गलियारे के पास एक काम है।**

segments.src: Instead of buying product by product, retailers group items the way shoppers think about them ("oral care," not "tubes we get from Colgate") and manage that group as a business unit.
segments.tr: उत्पाद दर उत्पाद खरीदने के बजाय, खुदरा विक्रेता वस्तुओं को उसी तरह समूहीकृत करते हैं जैसे खरीदार उन्हें सोचते हैं ("मौखिक देखभाल," न कि "ट्यूब जो हमें Colgate से मिलते हैं") और उस समूह को एक व्यावसायिक इकाई के रूप में प्रबंधित करते हैं।

segments.src: The framework, popularized in the 1990s through the industry's Efficient Consumer Response push, starts by assigning each category a **role**:
segments.tr: यह ढांचा, 1990 के दशक में उद्योग के कुशल उपभोक्ता प्रतिक्रिया पुश के माध्यम से लोकप्रिय, प्रत्येक श्रेणी को एक **भूमिका** निर्दिष्ट करके शुरू होता है:

segments.src: - **Destination** — a reason to choose this store over the one down the road. Deep assortment, sharp prices, lots of space.
segments.tr: - **गंतव्य** — इस स्टोर को सड़क के नीचे वाले के बजाय चुनने का कारण। गहरी श्रेणी, तीव्र कीमतें, बहुत सारी जगह।

segments.src: - **Routine** — the everyday workhorse that builds the basket and carries margin. Most of the store lives here.
segments.tr: - **दिनचर्या** — रोजमर्रा का कार्य घोड़ा जो टोकरी बनाता है और मार्जिन ले जाता है। स्टोर का अधिकांश यहाँ रहता है।

segments.src: - **Occasional / seasonal** — grilling supplies in June, school glue in August.
segments.tr: - **कभी-कभी / मौसमी** — जून में ग्रिलिंग आपूर्ति, अगस्त में स्कूल गोंद।

segments.src: - **Convenience** — you didn't come for it, but it's there. Fewer options, healthier margins.
segments.tr: - **सुविधा** — आप इसके लिए नहीं आए, लेकिन यह यहाँ है। कम विकल्प, स्वस्थ मार्जिन।

segments.src: The role drives everything downstream: how many SKUs, how much shelf, how aggressive the price, how much promo money.
segments.tr: भूमिका सब कुछ को आगे बढ़ाती है: कितने SKU, कितनी शेल्फ, कीमत कितनी आक्रामक है, कितना प्रचार पैसा है।

segments.src: A destination category and a convenience category get opposite treatment on purpose.
segments.tr: एक गंतव्य श्रेणी और एक सुविधा श्रेणी को जानबूझकर विपरीत उपचार मिलता है।

segments.src: One wrinkle worth knowing: retailers often name a **category captain** — usually the biggest supplier — to help build the plan, since that vendor has the best data.
segments.tr: जानने लायक एक झुर्री: खुदरा विक्रेता अक्सर एक **श्रेणी कप्तान** — आमतौर पर सबसे बड़ा आपूर्तिकर्ता — को नाम देते हैं योजना बनाने में मदद करने के लिए, क्योंकि उस विक्रेता के पास सर्वोत्तम डेटा है।

segments.src: It's efficient and it's a conflict of interest at the same time, which is why captains' recommendations get audited and why the practice draws antitrust attention.
segments.tr: यह कुशल है और यह एक ही समय में हित का टकराव है, यही कारण है कि कप्तानों की सिफारिशों का ऑडिट किया जाता है और यह प्रथा एंटीट्रस्ट ध्यान आकर्षित करती है।

segments.src: Inventory management — the shelf is a bank account.**
segments.tr: इन्वेंटरी प्रबंधन — शेल्फ एक बैंक खाता है।**

segments.src: Every unit on that shelf is cash the retailer can't use for anything else.
segments.tr: उस शेल्फ पर हर इकाई नकद है जिसे खुदरा विक्रेता किसी और चीज़ के लिए नहीं ले सकता।

segments.src: So the question isn't "did it sell?"
segments.tr: तो सवाल यह नहीं है कि "क्या यह बिका?"

segments.src: but "what did it earn per dollar tied up?"
segments.tr: बल्कि "क्या यह बंधी हुई प्रति डॉलर कमाई था?"

segments.src: Two numbers carry the load:
segments.tr: दो संख्याएं भार ले जाती हैं:

segments.src: inventory turnover = cost of goods sold / average inventory at cost
segments.tr: inventory turnover = cost of goods sold / average inventory at cost

segments.src: GMROI = gross margin dollars / average inventory at cost
segments.tr: GMROI = gross margin dollars / average inventory at cost

segments.src: weeks of supply = 52 / annual turns
segments.tr: weeks of supply = 52 / annual turns

segments.src: GMROI of 2.5 means the category returned $2.50 of gross margin for every $1 invested in inventory.
segments.tr: 2.5 की GMROI का मतलब है कि श्रेणी इन्वेंटरी में निवेश किए गए प्रत्येक $1 के लिए $2.50 सकल मार्जिन लौटाई।

segments.src: This is why a low-margin item that turns 20 times a year can beat a high-margin item that turns twice — and why buyers argue about turns more than about markup.
segments.tr: यही कारण है कि एक कम मार्जिन वाली वस्तु जो साल में 20 बार घूमती है, एक उच्च मार्जिन वाली वस्तु को हरा सकती है जो दो बार घूमती है — और यही कारण है कि खरीदार मार्कअप की तुलना में अधिक घूमता हुआ बहस करते हैं।

segments.src: The counterweight is service level.
segments.tr: प्रतिभार सेवा स्तर है।

segments.src: Order less and you free cash but risk an out-of-stock, which costs the sale and sometimes the trip.
segments.tr: कम आदेश दें और आप नकद मुक्त करें लेकिन एक स्टॉक से बाहर का जोखिम, जो बिक्री की लागत है और कभी-कभी यात्रा।

segments.src: So teams hold **safety stock** and set a reorder point:
segments.tr: तो टीमें **सुरक्षा स्टॉक** रखते हैं और एक पुनः आदेश बिंदु निर्धारित करते हैं:

segments.src: reorder point = expected demand during lead time + safety stock
segments.tr: reorder point = expected demand during lead time + safety stock

segments.src: Then there's leakage.
segments.tr: फिर रिसाव है।

segments.src: **Shrink** — theft, damage, spoilage, paperwork errors — has run around 1.5% of sales in recent National Retail Federation security surveys.
segments.tr: **सिकुड़न** — चोरी, क्षति, खराब होना, कागजी त्रुटियां — हाल के राष्ट्रीय खुदरा संघ सुरक्षा सर्वेक्षणों में बिक्री के लगभग 1.5% रही है।

segments.src: On thin retail margins, that's not rounding.
segments.tr: पतले खुदरा मार्जिन पर, यह गोलाई नहीं है।

segments.src: Pricing — margin and image, at the same time.**
segments.tr: मूल्य निर्धारण — मार्जिन और छवि, एक ही समय में।**

segments.src: The arithmetic is easy:
segments.tr: अंकगणित आसान है:

segments.src: retail price = cost / (1 - target margin %)
segments.tr: retail price = cost / (1 - target margin %)

segments.src: "Keystone" markup just means doubling cost: a $5 item retails at $10, a 50% margin.
segments.tr: "कीस्टोन" मार्कअप का मतलब है कि लागत को दोगुना करना: एक $5 की वस्तु $10 में खुदरा विक्रय होती है, 50% मार्जिन।

segments.src: The strategy is the hard part, and it splits two ways.
segments.tr: रणनीति कठिन हिस्सा है, और यह दो तरीकों से विभाजित होती है।

segments.src: **EDLP** (everyday low price) keeps prices flat and predictable — Walmart, Costco, Aldi.
segments.tr: **EDLP** (रोजमर्रा की कम कीमत) कीमतों को समतल और अनुमानित रखता है — Walmart, Costco, Aldi।

segments.src: **High–low** runs a base price plus frequent, deep promotions, often gated behind a loyalty card — most conventional supermarkets and department stores.
segments.tr: **उच्च–निम्न** एक आधार कीमत और बार-बार, गहरे प्रचार चलाता है, अक्सर एक लॉयल्टी कार्ड के पीछे द्वार — अधिकांश पारंपरिक सुपरमार्केट और डिपार्टमेंट स्टोर।

segments.src: EDLP smooths demand and cuts labor spent re-ticketing; high–low creates urgency and pulls in deal-sensitive shoppers, at the cost of training people to wait for the sale.
segments.tr: EDLP मांग को सुगम करता है और पुनः टिकट पर खर्च किए गए श्रम को काटता है; उच्च–निम्न तात्कालिकता बनाता है और सौदे-संवेदनशील खरीदारों को खींचता है, लोगों को बिक्री के लिए प्रतीक्षा करने के लिए प्रशिक्षित करने की कीमत पर।

segments.src: Either way, no one prices 40,000 items with equal care.
segments.tr: किसी भी तरह से, कोई भी 40,000 वस्तुओं को समान देखभाल के साथ कीमत नहीं देता है।

segments.src: Shoppers only remember a few dozen **key value items** — milk, eggs, bananas, a 12-pack of soda — and those set the store's price image.
segments.tr: खरीदार केवल कुछ दर्जन **मुख्य मूल्य वस्तुओं** को याद रखते हैं — दूध, अंडे, केले, सोडा का 12-पैक — और जो स्टोर की कीमत छवि निर्धारित करते हैं।

segments.src: Those get priced sharply, sometimes at or below cost as a **loss leader**, and the margin is recovered on the rest of the basket.
segments.tr: उन्हें तीव्रता से कीमत दी जाती है, कभी-कभी एक **हानि नेता** के रूप में लागत पर या उससे नीचे, और मार्जिन को शेष टोकरी पर पुनर्प्राप्त किया जाता है।

segments.src: (Loss leaders are generally legal, though a number of states have minimum-markup laws, usually covering gas, alcohol, or tobacco.)
segments.tr: (हानि नेता आमतौर पर कानूनी होते हैं, हालांकि कई राज्यों में न्यूनतम-मार्कअप कानून होते हैं, आमतौर पर गैस, शराब, या तंबाकू को कवर करते हैं।)

segments.src: And when inventory ages, **markdowns** are the release valve: a planned cadence of cuts that converts stale stock back into cash before it's worth nothing.
segments.tr: और जब इन्वेंटरी उम्र की होती है, **मार्कडाउन** रिलीज वाल्व होते हैं: कटों का एक नियोजित संचार जो पुरानी स्टॉक को यह कुछ भी न होने से पहले नकद में वापस परिवर्तित करता है।

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## रोजमर्रा की जिंदगी में

segments.src: Sunday morning, a Kroger on the north side of Columbus.
segments.tr: रविवार सुबह, कोलंबस के उत्तरी तरफ एक Kroger।

segments.src: Your cart: a gallon of milk, cereal, toothpaste, tortilla chips, a rotisserie chicken.
segments.tr: आपकी कार्ट: दूध का एक गैलन, अनाज, टूथपेस्ट, तोरतिल्ला चिप्स, एक रोटिसरी चिकन।

segments.src: The milk is a key value item.
segments.tr: दूध एक मुख्य मूल्य वस्तु है।

segments.src: It's priced within pennies of the Meijer two miles away because management assumes you know roughly what milk costs.
segments.tr: यह Meijer के दो मील दूर के पेनी के भीतर कीमत दी जाती है क्योंकि प्रबंधन मानता है कि आप जानते हैं कि दूध की कीमत लगभग क्या है।

segments.src: The rotisserie chicken is close to a loss leader — cooked from a bird that would've been marked down anyway, priced to get you through the door on the one trip where you might also buy a $30 cut of steak.
segments.tr: रोटिसरी चिकन एक हानि नेता के करीब है — एक पक्षी से पकाया गया जो वैसे भी मार्क डाउन किया जाता, आपको दरवाजे के माध्यम से प्राप्त करने के लिए कीमत, उस एक यात्रा पर जहां आप स्टीक के एक $30 कट भी खरीद सकते हैं।

segments.src: Costco has famously held its chicken at $4.99 for years for exactly this reason.
segments.tr: Costco ने प्रसिद्धि से अपनी चिकन को $4.99 पर वर्षों तक इसी कारण से रखा है।

segments.src: The toothpaste tells the category story.
segments.tr: टूथपेस्ट श्रेणी की कहानी बताता है।

segments.src: Oral care is a routine category here, so you get maybe 40 SKUs, not 90, and the shelf runs a familiar pattern: a national brand at eye level, the Kroger store brand right beside it at a lower price and a higher margin, and the $9 whitening kit on the top shelf where it turns slowly but earns well when it does.
segments.tr: मौखिक देखभाल यहाँ एक दिनचर्या श्रेणी है, इसलिए आप शायद 40 SKU प्राप्त करते हैं, 90 नहीं, और शेल्फ एक परिचित पैटर्न चलाता है: आँख के स्तर पर एक राष्ट्रीय ब्रांड, Kroger स्टोर ब्रांड इसके ठीक बगल में एक कम कीमत और एक उच्च मार्जिन पर, और $9 की सफेदी किट शीर्ष शेल्फ पर जहां यह धीरे-धीरे घूमता है लेकिन अच्छी तरह से कमाता है जब यह होता है।

segments.src: The chips are near the front — high turns, decent margin, impulse-friendly placement.
segments.tr: चिप्स सामने के पास हैं — उच्च घूमता है, सभ्य मार्जिन, आवेग-अनुकूल प्लेसमेंट।

segments.src: And the endcap you walked past with the seasonal cooler display?
segments.tr: और एंडकैप जिसे आप मौसमी कूलर डिस्प्ले के साथ पास कर गए?

segments.src: That's an occasional category, bought in a single seasonal buy, with a markdown schedule already written for late August.
segments.tr: यह एक कभी-कभी श्रेणी है, एक एकल मौसमी खरीद में खरीदी गई, अगस्त के अंत के लिए पहले से लिखा गया एक मार्कडाउन शेड्यूल के साथ।

segments.src: Nobody will scramble when it stops selling.
segments.tr: जब यह बिक्री करना बंद कर देता है तो कोई भी झगड़ा नहीं करेगा।

segments.src: That was the plan in April.
segments.tr: वह अप्रैल में योजना थी।

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## तीन-पंक्ति पुनरावृत्ति

segments.src: 1. Category management treats each group of products as a business with an assigned role — destination, routine, occasional, or convenience — and that role drives assortment, space, and price aggressiveness.
segments.tr: 1. श्रेणी प्रबंधन उत्पादों के प्रत्येक समूह को एक निर्दिष्ट भूमिका के साथ एक व्यवसाय के रूप में मानता है — गंतव्य, दिनचर्या, कभी-कभी, या सुविधा — और वह भूमिका श्रेणी, स्थान, और कीमत की आक्रामकता को चलाती है।

segments.src: 2. Inventory is capital, so retailers judge it by turns and GMROI (gross margin per dollar invested), balancing that against the cost of being out of stock.
segments.tr: 2. इन्वेंटरी पूंजी है, इसलिए खुदरा विक्रेता इसे घूमता हुआ और GMROI (निवेश किए गए प्रति डॉलर सकल मार्जिन) द्वारा न्याय करते हैं, इसे स्टॉक से बाहर होने की लागत के विरुद्ध संतुलित करते हैं।

segments.src: 3. Pricing is a portfolio: sharp on the handful of key value items that shape price image, and recovered across everything else — under either an EDLP or a high–low strategy.
segments.tr: 3. मूल्य निर्धारण एक पोर्टफोलियो है: कई मुख्य मूल्य वस्तुओं पर तीव्र जो मूल्य छवि को आकार देते हैं, और बाकी सब कुछ में पुनर्प्राप्त — या तो EDLP या उच्च–निम्न रणनीति के तहत।

segments.src: ## ✅ Self Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ स्व परीक्षा

segments.src: **1.** A category posts a GMROI of 3.0.
segments.tr: **1.** एक श्रेणी 3.0 की GMROI पोस्ट करती है।

segments.src: What does that mean?
segments.tr: इसका क्या मतलब है?

segments.src: A) It sold three times more than last year
segments.tr: A) इसने पिछले साल की तुलना में तीन गुना अधिक बिकी

segments.src: B) It earned $3.00 of gross margin per $1 invested in inventory at cost
segments.tr: B) इसने लागत पर इन्वेंटरी में निवेश किए गए प्रति $1 के $3.00 सकल मार्जिन अर्जित किए

segments.src: C) Its gross margin is 30%
segments.tr: C) इसका सकल मार्जिन 30% है

segments.src: D) It turns three times per week
segments.tr: D) यह सप्ताह में तीन बार घूमता है

segments.src: **2.** O / X — An EDLP retailer's core strategy is running deep weekly promotions to create urgency.
segments.tr: **2.** O / X — एक EDLP खुदरा विक्रेता की मूल रणनीति तात्कालिकता बनाने के लिए गहरे साप्ताहिक प्रचार चला रही है।

segments.src: **3.** In a supermarket, "milk and eggs, priced to match the competitor down the street" is best described as:
segments.tr: **3.** एक सुपरमार्केट में, "दूध और अंडे, कीमत सड़क के नीचे प्रतियोगी से मेल खाने के लिए" सबसे अच्छा वर्णित है:

segments.src: A) A convenience category

segments.src: B) A seasonal buy

es.title: [Retailing 101 #9] Cada pasillo es un pequeño negocio y tiene su propio P&L

segments.src: > One-line summary: Advanced merchandising means running each category like a standalone business — giving it a job to do, measuring the return on the cash parked in its inventory, and setting prices that protect both margin and price image.
segments.tr: > Resumen de una línea: La comercialización avanzada significa ejecutar cada categoría como un negocio independiente, asignándole un objetivo, midiendo el retorno sobre el efectivo invertido en su inventario y estableciendo precios que protejan tanto el margen como la imagen de precio.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Concepto de hoy

segments.src: Last time we met the person who picked everything on the shelf six months before you walked in.
segments.tr: La última vez conocimos a la persona que eligió todo lo que hay en el estante seis meses antes de que entrara.

segments.src: Today: how they actually decide.
segments.tr: Hoy: cómo lo deciden realmente.

segments.src: Three levers do most of the work.
segments.tr: Tres palancas hacen la mayor parte del trabajo.

segments.src: Category management — the aisle has a job.**
segments.tr: Gestión de categorías — el pasillo tiene un objetivo.**

segments.src: Instead of buying product by product, retailers group items the way shoppers think about them ("oral care," not "tubes we get from Colgate") and manage that group as a business unit.
segments.tr: En lugar de comprar producto por producto, los minoristas agrupan artículos de la forma en que los compradores los ven ("cuidado oral", no "tubos que obtenemos de Colgate") y gestionan ese grupo como una unidad comercial.

segments.src: The framework, popularized in the 1990s through the industry's Efficient Consumer Response push, starts by assigning each category a **role**:
segments.tr: El marco, popularizado en los años 90 a través del esfuerzo de Respuesta Eficiente al Consumidor de la industria, comienza asignando a cada categoría un **rol**:

segments.src: - **Destination** — a reason to choose this store over the one down the road. Deep assortment, sharp prices, lots of space.
segments.tr: - **Destino** — una razón para elegir esta tienda en lugar de la de abajo. Surtido profundo, precios competitivos, mucho espacio.

segments.src: - **Routine** — the everyday workhorse that builds the basket and carries margin. Most of the store lives here.
segments.tr: - **Rutina** — el caballo de batalla cotidiano que construye el carrito y genera margen. La mayoría de la tienda está aquí.

segments.src: - **Occasional / seasonal** — grilling supplies in June, school glue in August.
segments.tr: - **Ocasional / estacional** — suministros para asar en junio, pegamento escolar en agosto.

segments.src: - **Convenience** — you didn't come for it, but it's there. Fewer options, healthier margins.
segments.tr: - **Conveniencia** — no viniste por ello, pero está ahí. Menos opciones, márgenes más saludables.

segments.src: The role drives everything downstream: how many SKUs, how much shelf, how aggressive the price, how much promo money.
segments.tr: El rol impulsa todo lo que viene después: cuántos SKU, cuánto espacio en estante, cuán agresivo es el precio, cuánto dinero de promoción.

segments.src: A destination category and a convenience category get opposite treatment on purpose.
segments.tr: Una categoría de destino y una categoría de conveniencia reciben tratamiento opuesto a propósito.

segments.src: One wrinkle worth knowing: retailers often name a **category captain** — usually the biggest supplier — to help build the plan, since that vendor has the best data.
segments.tr: Un matiz que vale la pena conocer: los minoristas a menudo nombran un **capitán de categoría** — generalmente el proveedor más grande — para ayudar a construir el plan, ya que ese vendedor tiene los mejores datos.

segments.src: It's efficient and it's a conflict of interest at the same time, which is why captains' recommendations get audited and why the practice draws antitrust attention.
segments.tr: Es eficiente y es un conflicto de intereses al mismo tiempo, por lo que las recomendaciones de los capitanes se auditan y por eso la práctica atrae atención antimonopolio.

segments.src: Inventory management — the shelf is a bank account.**
segments.tr: Gestión de inventario — el estante es una cuenta bancaria.**

segments.src: Every unit on that shelf is cash the retailer can't use for anything else.
segments.tr: Cada unidad en ese estante es efectivo que el minorista no puede usar para nada más.

segments.src: So the question isn't "did it sell?"
segments.tr: Así que la pregunta no es "¿se vendió?"

segments.src: but "what did it earn per dollar tied up?"
segments.tr: sino "¿qué ganó por dólar invertido?"

segments.src: Two numbers carry the load:
segments.tr: Dos números llevan la carga:

segments.src: inventory turnover = cost of goods sold / average inventory at cost
segments.tr: inventory turnover = cost of goods sold / average inventory at cost

segments.src: GMROI = gross margin dollars / average inventory at cost
segments.tr: GMROI = gross margin dollars / average inventory at cost

segments.src: weeks of supply = 52 / annual turns
segments.tr: weeks of supply = 52 / annual turns

segments.src: GMROI of 2.5 means the category returned $2.50 of gross margin for every $1 invested in inventory.
segments.tr: Un GMROI de 2,5 significa que la categoría devolvió $2,50 de margen bruto por cada $1 invertido en inventario.

segments.src: This is why a low-margin item that turns 20 times a year can beat a high-margin item that turns twice — and why buyers argue about turns more than about markup.
segments.tr: Esta es la razón por la que un artículo de bajo margen que se vende 20 veces al año puede vencer a un artículo de alto margen que se vende dos veces — y por eso los compradores debaten más sobre rotaciones que sobre margen.

segments.src: The counterweight is service level.
segments.tr: El contrapeso es el nivel de servicio.

segments.src: Order less and you free cash but risk an out-of-stock, which costs the sale and sometimes the trip.
segments.tr: Pedir menos y liberar efectivo pero arriesgar un desabastecimiento, que cuesta la venta y a veces el viaje.

segments.src: So teams hold **safety stock** and set a reorder point:
segments.tr: Así que los equipos mantienen **existencias de seguridad** y establecen un punto de reorden:

segments.src: reorder point = expected demand during lead time + safety stock
segments.tr: reorder point = expected demand during lead time + safety stock

segments.src: Then there's leakage.
segments.tr: Luego está la fuga.

segments.src: **Shrink** — theft, damage, spoilage, paperwork errors — has run around 1.5% of sales in recent National Retail Federation security surveys.
segments.tr: **Encogimiento** — robo, daño, deterioro, errores de papeleo — ha rondado el 1,5% de las ventas en encuestas de seguridad recientes de la Federación Nacional de Minoristas.

segments.src: On thin retail margins, that's not rounding.
segments.tr: Con márgenes minoristas delgados, eso no es redondeo.

segments.src: Pricing — margin and image, at the same time.**
segments.tr: Precios — margen e imagen, al mismo tiempo.**

segments.src: The arithmetic is easy:
segments.tr: La aritmética es fácil:

segments.src: retail price = cost / (1 - target margin %)
segments.tr: retail price = cost / (1 - target margin %)

segments.src: "Keystone" markup just means doubling cost: a $5 item retails at $10, a 50% margin.
segments.tr: El margen "piedra angular" simplemente significa duplicar el costo: un artículo de $5 se vende al por menor a $10, un margen del 50%.

segments.src: The strategy is the hard part, and it splits two ways.
segments.tr: La estrategia es la parte difícil, y se divide de dos maneras.

segments.src: **EDLP** (everyday low price) keeps prices flat and predictable — Walmart, Costco, Aldi.
segments.tr: **EDLP** (precio diario bajo) mantiene los precios planos y predecibles — Walmart, Costco, Aldi.

segments.src: **High–low** runs a base price plus frequent, deep promotions, often gated behind a loyalty card — most conventional supermarkets and department stores.
segments.tr: **Alto-bajo** ejecuta un precio base más promociones frecuentes y profundas, a menudo limitadas detrás de una tarjeta de fidelización — la mayoría de supermercados convencionales y tiendas departamentales.

segments.src: EDLP smooths demand and cuts labor spent re-ticketing; high–low creates urgency and pulls in deal-sensitive shoppers, at the cost of training people to wait for the sale.
segments.tr: EDLP suaviza la demanda y reduce el trabajo de re-etiquetar; alto-bajo crea urgencia y atrae compradores sensibles a las ofertas, al costo de entrenar a las personas a esperar la venta.

segments.src: Either way, no one prices 40,000 items with equal care.
segments.tr: De cualquier forma, nadie fija precios en 40.000 artículos con igual cuidado.

segments.src: Shoppers only remember a few dozen **key value items** — milk, eggs, bananas, a 12-pack of soda — and those set the store's price image.
segments.tr: Los compradores solo recuerdan algunas docenas de **artículos clave de valor** — leche, huevos, plátanos, un paquete de 12 refrescos — y esos fijan la imagen de precio de la tienda.

segments.src: Those get priced sharply, sometimes at or below cost as a **loss leader**, and the margin is recovered on the rest of the basket.
segments.tr: Esos se cotizan fuertemente, a veces a costo o por debajo como un **articulo de pérdida**, y el margen se recupera en el resto del carrito.

segments.src: (Loss leaders are generally legal, though a number of states have minimum-markup laws, usually covering gas, alcohol, or tobacco.)
segments.tr: (Los artículos de pérdida son generalmente legales, aunque varios estados tienen leyes de margen mínimo, generalmente que cubren gasolina, alcohol o tabaco.)

segments.src: And when inventory ages, **markdowns** are the release valve: a planned cadence of cuts that converts stale stock back into cash before it's worth nothing.
segments.tr: Y cuando el inventario envejece, **rebajas** son la válvula de escape: un ritmo planificado de recortes que convierte existencias obsoletas de nuevo en efectivo antes de que valga nada.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## En la vida cotidiana

segments.src: Sunday morning, a Kroger on the north side of Columbus.
segments.tr: Domingo por la mañana, un Kroger en el norte de Columbus.

segments.src: Your cart: a gallon of milk, cereal, toothpaste, tortilla chips, a rotisserie chicken.
segments.tr: Tu carrito: un galón de leche, cereal, pasta de dientes, chips de tortilla, un pollo a la brasa.

segments.src: The milk is a key value item.
segments.tr: La leche es un artículo clave de valor.

segments.src: It's priced within pennies of the Meijer two miles away because management assumes you know roughly what milk costs.
segments.tr: Se cotiza dentro de centavos del Meijer a dos millas de distancia porque la gerencia asume que sabes aproximadamente cuánto cuesta la leche.

segments.src: The rotisserie chicken is close to a loss leader — cooked from a bird that would've been marked down anyway, priced to get you through the door on the one trip where you might also buy a $30 cut of steak.
segments.tr: El pollo a la brasa está cerca de un artículo de pérdida — cocinado de un ave que habría sido marcada a la baja de todos modos, con precio para hacerte entrar por la puerta en el viaje en el que también podrías comprar un corte de $30 de carne.

segments.src: Costco has famously held its chicken at $4.99 for years for exactly this reason.
segments.tr: Costco ha mantenido famosamente su pollo a $4,99 durante años por exactamente esta razón.

segments.src: The toothpaste tells the category story.
segments.tr: La pasta de dientes cuenta la historia de la categoría.

segments.src: Oral care is a routine category here, so you get maybe 40 SKUs, not 90, and the shelf runs a familiar pattern: a national brand at eye level, the Kroger store brand right beside it at a lower price and a higher margin, and the $9 whitening kit on the top shelf where it turns slowly but earns well when it does.
segments.tr: El cuidado oral es una categoría de rutina aquí, así que obtienes tal vez 40 SKU, no 90, y el estante ejecuta un patrón familiar: una marca nacional a la altura de los ojos, la marca de la tienda Kroger justo al lado a un precio más bajo y un margen más alto, y el kit blanqueador de $9 en el estante superior donde se vende lentamente pero gana bien cuando lo hace.

segments.src: The chips are near the front — high turns, decent margin, impulse-friendly placement.
segments.tr: Los chips están cerca del frente — rotaciones altas, margen decente, ubicación amigable con los impulsos.

segments.src: And the endcap you walked past with the seasonal cooler display?
segments.tr: ¿Y el extremo que pasaste con la pantalla del enfriador estacional?

segments.src: That's an occasional category, bought in a single seasonal buy, with a markdown schedule already written for late August.
segments.tr: Esa es una categoría ocasional, comprada en una sola compra estacional, con un cronograma de rebajas ya escrito para finales de agosto.

segments.src: Nobody will scramble when it stops selling.
segments.tr: Nadie se apresurará cuando deje de vender.

segments.src: That was the plan in April.
segments.tr: Ese fue el plan en abril.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Resumen de tres líneas

segments.src: 1. Category management treats each group of products as a business with an assigned role — destination, routine, occasional, or convenience — and that role drives assortment, space, and price aggressiveness.
segments.tr: 1. La gestión de categorías trata cada grupo de productos como un negocio con un rol asignado — destino, rutina, ocasional o conveniencia — y ese rol impulsa el surtido, el espacio y la agresividad de precios.

segments.src: 2. Inventory is capital, so retailers judge it by turns and GMROI (gross margin per dollar invested), balancing that against the cost of being out of stock.
segments.tr: 2. El inventario es capital, por lo que los minoristas lo juzgan por rotaciones y GMROI (margen bruto por dólar invertido), equilibrando eso contra el costo de estar sin existencias.

segments.src: 3. Pricing is a portfolio: sharp on the handful of key value items that shape price image, and recovered across everything else — under either an EDLP or a high–low strategy.
segments.tr: 3. Los precios son una cartera: agresivos en el puñado de artículos clave de valor que moldean la imagen de precio, y recuperados en todo lo demás — bajo una estrategia EDLP o alto-bajo.

segments.tr: - **Gestión de categorías** — Gestión de un grupo de productos relacionados como una unidad comercial única con su propio rol, estrategia y cuadro de mando, en lugar de artículo por artículo.

segments.src: - **Category role** — The job assigned to a category (destination, routine, occasional/seasonal, convenience), which determines its space, assortment breadth, and pricing posture.
segments.tr: - **Rol de categoría** — El trabajo asignado a una categoría (destino, rutina, ocasional/estacional, conveniencia), que determina su espacio, amplitud de surtido y postura de precios.

segments.src: - **GMROI** — Gross margin return on inventory investment: gross margin dollars divided by average inventory at cost; the profit earned per dollar tied up in stock.

segments.src: - **Inventory turnover** — How many times a year inventory is sold and replaced (COGS ÷ average inventory at cost); higher turns free up cash and reduce markdown risk.
segments.tr: - **Rotación de inventario** — Cuántas veces al año se vende y se reemplaza el inventario (COGS ÷ inventario promedio a costo); las rotaciones más altas liberan efectivo y reducen el riesgo de rebajas.

segments.src: - **EDLP vs. high–low** — Two pricing strategies: consistently low everyday prices, versus a higher base price punctuated by frequent deep promotions.
segments.tr: - **EDLP vs. alto-bajo** — Dos estrategias de precios: precios bajos diarios consistentemente bajos, versus un precio base más alto punteado por promociones profundas frecuentes.

segments.tr: > ملخص سطر واحد: التجارة المتقدمة تعني إدارة كل فئة مثل عمل مستقل — إعطاؤها مهمة لتؤديها، وقياس العائد على النقد المحتفظ به في مخزونها، وتحديد الأسعار التي تحمي كلاً من الهامش وصورة السعر.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## مفهوم اليوم

segments.src: Last time we met the person who picked everything on the shelf six months before you walked in.
segments.tr: في المرة الماضية التقينا بالشخص الذي اختار كل شيء على الرف قبل ستة أشهر من دخولك.

segments.src: Today: how they actually decide.
segments.tr: اليوم: كيف يقررون فعلياً.

segments.src: Three levers do most of the work.
segments.tr: ثلاثة روافع تقوم معظم العمل.

segments.src: Category management — the aisle has a job.**
segments.tr: إدارة الفئة — للممر مهمة.**

segments.src: Instead of buying product by product, retailers group items the way shoppers think about them ("oral care," not "tubes we get from Colgate") and manage that group as a business unit.
segments.tr: بدلاً من شراء المنتج تلو الآخر، تجميع بائعي التجزئة العناصر بالطريقة التي يفكر بها المتسوقون ("العناية بالفم،" وليس "الأنابيب التي نحصل عليها من كولجيت") وإدارة تلك المجموعة كوحدة عمل.

segments.src: The framework, popularized in the 1990s through the industry's Efficient Consumer Response push, starts by assigning each category a **role**:
segments.tr: يبدأ الإطار، الذي حظي بشهرة في التسعينيات من خلال دفع الصناعة نحو الاستجابة الفعالة للمستهلك، بتعيين كل فئة **دوراً**:

segments.src: - **Destination** — a reason to choose this store over the one down the road. Deep assortment, sharp prices, lots of space.
segments.tr: - **الوجهة** — سبب لاختيار هذا المتجر بدلاً من الذي على الطريق. مجموعة شاملة، أسعار حادة، مساحة كبيرة.

segments.src: - **Routine** — the everyday workhorse that builds the basket and carries margin. Most of the store lives here.
segments.tr: - **الروتين** — العامل اليومي الموثوق الذي يبني السلة ويحمل الهامش. معظم المتجر يوجد هنا.

segments.src: - **Occasional / seasonal** — grilling supplies in June, school glue in August.
segments.tr: - **العرضي / الموسمي** — مستلزمات الشواء في يونيو، غراء الدرسة في أغسطس.

segments.src: - **Convenience** — you didn't come for it, but it's there. Fewer options, healthier margins.
segments.tr: - **الراحة** — لم تأتِ لأجله، لكنه هنا. خيارات أقل، هوامش أصحّ.

segments.src: The role drives everything downstream: how many SKUs, how much shelf, how aggressive the price, how much promo money.
segments.tr: يحرك الدور كل شيء في اتجاه مجرى النهر: عدد وحدات الحفظ، مقدار الرف، مدى عدوانية السعر، مقدار أموال الترويج.

segments.src: A destination category and a convenience category get opposite treatment on purpose.
segments.tr: فئة الوجهة وفئة الراحة يحصلان على معاملة معاكسة عن قصد.

segments.src: One wrinkle worth knowing: retailers often name a **category captain** — usually the biggest supplier — to help build the plan, since that vendor has the best data.
segments.tr: هناك تجعد واحد يستحق المعرفة: غالباً ما يعيّن بائعو التجزئة **قائد الفئة** — عادة أكبر مورّد — للمساعدة في بناء الخطة، لأن ذلك البائع لديه أفضل البيانات.

segments.src: It's efficient and it's a conflict of interest at the same time, which is why captains' recommendations get audited and why the practice draws antitrust attention.
segments.tr: إنها فعالة وهي تضارب مصالح في نفس الوقت، وهذا هو السبب في أن توصيات القادة يتم تدقيقها ولماذا تجذب الممارسة اهتمام مكافحة الاحتكار.

segments.src: Inventory management — the shelf is a bank account.**
segments.tr: إدارة الجرد — الرف حساب بنكي.**

segments.src: Every unit on that shelf is cash the retailer can't use for anything else.
segments.tr: كل وحدة على ذلك الرف هي نقود لا يستطيع بائع التجزئة استخدامها لأي شيء آخر.

segments.src: So the question isn't "did it sell?"
segments.tr: لذا فإن السؤال ليس "هل باع؟"

segments.src: but "what did it earn per dollar tied up?"
segments.tr: بل "ماذا كسب لكل دولار محتفظ به؟"

segments.src: Two numbers carry the load:
segments.tr: رقمان يحملان الحمل:

segments.src: inventory turnover = cost of goods sold / average inventory at cost
segments.tr: inventory turnover = cost of goods sold / average inventory at cost

segments.src: GMROI = gross margin dollars / average inventory at cost
segments.tr: GMROI = gross margin dollars / average inventory at cost

segments.src: weeks of supply = 52 / annual turns
segments.tr: weeks of supply = 52 / annual turns

segments.src: GMROI of 2.5 means the category returned $2.50 of gross margin for every $1 invested in inventory.
segments.tr: GMROI من 2.5 يعني أن الفئة حققت 2.50 دولار من الهامش الإجمالي لكل دولار مستثمر في الجرد.

segments.src: This is why a low-margin item that turns 20 times a year can beat a high-margin item that turns twice — and why buyers argue about turns more than about markup.
segments.tr: وهذا هو السبب في أن عنصراً بهامش منخفض يدور 20 مرة في السنة يمكن أن يتفوق على عنصر بهامش مرتفع يدور مرتين — وسبب جدل المشترين حول الدورات أكثر من الترميز.

segments.src: The counterweight is service level.
segments.tr: الثقل المقابل هو مستوى الخدمة.

segments.src: Order less and you free cash but risk an out-of-stock, which costs the sale and sometimes the trip.
segments.tr: اطلب أقل وأنت تحرر النقد لكن تخاطر بانقطاع المخزون، مما يكلف البيع وأحياناً الرحلة.

segments.src: So teams hold **safety stock** and set a reorder point:
segments.tr: لذا تحتفظ الفرق **بمخزون الأمان** وتحدد نقطة إعادة الطلب:

segments.src: reorder point = expected demand during lead time + safety stock
segments.tr: reorder point = expected demand during lead time + safety stock

segments.src: Then there's leakage.
segments.tr: ثم هناك تسرب.

segments.src: **Shrink** — theft, damage, spoilage, paperwork errors — has run around 1.5% of sales in recent National Retail Federation security surveys.
segments.tr: **الانكماش** — السرقة والأضرار والتلف وأخطاء الورقية — قد جرت حول 1.5٪ من المبيعات في استطلاعات الأمان الحديثة للاتحاد الوطني لبائعي التجزئة.

segments.src: On thin retail margins, that's not rounding.
segments.tr: على هوامش البيع بالتجزئة الرقيقة، هذا ليس تقريباً.

segments.src: Pricing — margin and image, at the same time.**
segments.tr: التسعير — الهامش والصورة، في نفس الوقت.**

segments.src: The arithmetic is easy:
segments.tr: الحسابات سهلة:

segments.src: retail price = cost / (1 - target margin %)
segments.tr: retail price = cost / (1 - target margin %)

segments.src: "Keystone" markup just means doubling cost: a $5 item retails at $10, a 50% margin.
segments.tr: "Keystone" ترميز يعني ببساطة مضاعفة التكلفة: عنصر 5 دولارات يُباع بـ 10 دولارات، هامش 50٪.

segments.src: The strategy is the hard part, and it splits two ways.
segments.tr: الاستراتيجية هي الجزء الصعب، وهي تنقسم بطريقتين.

segments.src: **EDLP** (everyday low price) keeps prices flat and predictable — Walmart, Costco, Aldi.
segments.tr: **EDLP** (السعر المنخفض اليومي) يحافظ على الأسعار مسطحة وقابلة للتنبؤ — Walmart و Costco و Aldi.

segments.src: **High–low** runs a base price plus frequent, deep promotions, often gated behind a loyalty card — most conventional supermarkets and department stores.
segments.tr: **مرتفع–منخفض** يدير سعر أساسي بالإضافة إلى عروض ترويجية متكررة وعميقة، غالباً محصورة خلف بطاقة الولاء — معظم محلات البقالة التقليدية وقسم الملابس.

segments.src: EDLP smooths demand and cuts labor spent re-ticketing; high–low creates urgency and pulls in deal-sensitive shoppers, at the cost of training people to wait for the sale.
segments.tr: يسلس EDLP الطلب وقطع العمل المنفق على إعادة التسعير؛ ينشئ high-low الإلحاح ويسحب المتسوقين الحساسين للصفقات، بتكلفة تدريب الناس على انتظار البيع.

segments.src: Either way, no one prices 40,000 items with equal care.
segments.tr: على أي حال، لا أحد يسعر 40،000 عنصر بعناية متساوية.

segments.src: Shoppers only remember a few dozen **key value items** — milk, eggs, bananas, a 12-pack of soda — and those set the store's price image.
segments.tr: يتذكر المتسوقون فقط بضع عشرات من **عناصر القيمة الرئيسية** — الحليب والبيض والموز وعلبة من 12 زجاجة من الصودا — وتلك تحدد صورة السعر في المتجر.

segments.src: Those get priced sharply, sometimes at or below cost as a **loss leader**, and the margin is recovered on the rest of the basket.
segments.tr: يتم تسعير تلك بحدة، وأحياناً بسعر أو أقل من التكلفة كـ **مفقود رائد**، ويتم استرجاع الهامش على بقية السلة.

segments.src: (Loss leaders are generally legal, though a number of states have minimum-markup laws, usually covering gas, alcohol, or tobacco.)
And when inventory ages, **markdowns** are the release valve: a planned cadence of cuts that converts stale stock back into cash before it's worth nothing.
segments.tr: وعندما يتقدم الجرد في العمر، **الخصومات** هي صمام الإفراج: إيقاع مخطط له من خفض تحويل المخزون الراكد إلى نقد قبل أن يكون بلا قيمة.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## في الحياة اليومية

segments.src: Sunday morning, a Kroger on the north side of Columbus.
segments.tr: صباح الأحد، Kroger على الجانب الشمالي من كولومبوس.

segments.src: Your cart: a gallon of milk, cereal, toothpaste, tortilla chips, a rotisserie chicken.
segments.tr: سلتك: جالون من الحليب، حبوب الإفطار، معجون الأسنان، رقائق التورتيلا، دجاجة مشوية.

segments.src: The milk is a key value item.
segments.tr: الحليب عنصر قيمة رئيسي.

segments.src: It's priced within pennies of the Meijer two miles away because management assumes you know roughly what milk costs.
segments.tr: يتم تسعيره ضمن فلسات من Meijer على بعد ميلين لأن الإدارة تفترض أنك تعرف تقريباً ما يكلف الحليب.

segments.src: The rotisserie chicken is close to a loss leader — cooked from a bird that would've been marked down anyway, priced to get you through the door on the one trip where you might also buy a $30 cut of steak.
segments.tr: الدجاجة المشوية قريبة من قائد خاسر — مطبوخة من طائر كان يتم تخفيض سعره على أي حال، بسعر للحصول عليك من خلال الباب في الرحلة الوحيدة حيث قد تشتري أيضاً قطعة لحم 30 دولار.

segments.src: Costco has famously held its chicken at $4.99 for years for exactly this reason.
segments.tr: ظلت Costco تحمل دجاجتها بسعر 4.99 دولار لسنوات لهذا السبب بالضبط.

segments.src: The toothpaste tells the category story.
segments.tr: معجون الأسنان يقول قصة الفئة.

segments.src: Oral care is a routine category here, so you get maybe 40 SKUs, not 90, and the shelf runs a familiar pattern: a national brand at eye level, the Kroger store brand right beside it at a lower price and a higher margin, and the $9 whitening kit on the top shelf where it turns slowly but earns well when it does.
segments.tr: العناية الفموية هي فئة روتينية هنا، لذا تحصل على ربما 40 وحدة حفظ، وليس 90، والرف يدير نمط مألوف: علامة تجارية وطنية على مستوى العين، ماركة كروجر الخاصة بك بجانبها مباشرة بسعر أقل وهامش أعلى، وحزمة تبييض 9 دولارات على الرف العلوي حيث تدور ببطء لكنها تربح جيداً عندما تفعل.

segments.src: The chips are near the front — high turns, decent margin, impulse-friendly placement.
segments.tr: الرقائق بالقرب من الأمام — دورات عالية، هامش لائق، موضع صديق للاندفاع.

segments.src: And the endcap you walked past with the seasonal cooler display?
segments.tr: والنقطة النهائية التي مررت بها مع عرض المبرد الموسمي؟

segments.src: That's an occasional category, bought in a single seasonal buy, with a markdown schedule already written for late August.
segments.tr: هذا فئة عرضية، تم شراؤها في عملية شراء موسمية واحدة، مع جدول خصم مكتوب بالفعل لنهاية أغسطس.

segments.src: Nobody will scramble when it stops selling.
segments.tr: لن يسارع أحد عندما يتوقف عن البيع.

segments.src: That was the plan in April.
segments.tr: كانت هذه الخطة في أبريل.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## ملخص من ثلاثة أسطر

segments.src: 1. Category management treats each group of products as a business with an assigned role — destination, routine, occasional, or convenience — and that role drives assortment, space, and price aggressiveness.
segments.tr: 1. تعامل إدارة الفئة كل مجموعة من المنتجات كعمل تجاري برول معين — وجهة أو روتين أو عرضي أو مريح — وهذا الدور يحرك الفرز والمساحة والعدوانية في السعر.

segments.src: 2. Inventory is capital, so retailers judge it by turns and GMROI (gross margin per dollar invested), balancing that against the cost of being out of stock.
segments.tr: 2. الجرد رأس مال، لذا يحكم على بائعو التجزئة من خلال الدورات و GMROI (الهامش الإجمالي لكل دولار مستثمر)، موازنة ذلك ضد تكلفة انقطاع المخزون.

segments.src: 3. Pricing is a portfolio: sharp on the handful of key value items that shape price image, and recovered across everything else — under either an EDLP or a high–low strategy.
segments.tr: 3. التسعير هو محفظة: حاد على حفنة من عناصر القيمة الرئيسية التي تشكل صورة السعر، ويتم استرجاعها عبر كل شيء آخر — تحت استراتيجية EDLP أو high-low.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ اختبار ذاتي

segments.tr: **1.** فئة تنشر GMROI من 3.0.

segments.src: What does that mean?
segments.tr: ماذا يعني ذلك؟

segments.src: A) It sold three times more than last year
segments.tr: A) باع ثلاث مرات أكثر من العام الماضي

segments.src: B) It earned $3.00 of gross margin per $1 invested in inventory at cost
segments.tr: B) كسب 3.00 دولار من الهامش الإجمالي لكل دولار مستثمر في الجرد بسعر التكلفة

segments.src: C) Its gross margin is 30%
segments.tr: C) الهامش الإجمالي الخاص به هو 30٪

segments.tr: D) يدور ثلاث مرات في الأسبوع

segments.tr: **2.** O / X — استراتيجية بائع البيع بالتجزئة الأساسية EDLP هي تشغيل عروض ترويجية عميقة أسبوعية لإنشاء إلحاح.

segments.src: **3.** In a supermarket, "milk and eggs, priced to match the competitor down the street" is best described as:
segments.tr: **3.** في محل بقالة، "الحليب والبيض، بسعر يطابق المنافس على الطريق" يُوصف بشكل أفضل بأنه:

segments.src: A) A convenience category
segments.tr: A) فئة الراحة

segments.tr: B) عملية شراء موسمية

segments.tr: C) عناصر قيمة رئيسية في دور الوجهة / جلب المرور

segments.tr: D) إيقاع خصم

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 شروط اليوم

segments.src: - **Category management** — Managing a group of related products as a single business unit with its own role, strategy, and scorecard, rather than item by item.
segments.tr: - **إدارة الفئة** — إدارة مجموعة من المنتجات ذات الصلة كوحدة عمل واحدة برول وإستراتيجية واستحقاق خاص بها، بدلاً من العنصر تلو العنصر.

segments.src: - **Category role** — The job assigned to a category (destination, routine, occasional/seasonal, convenience), which determines its space, assortment breadth, and pricing posture.
segments.tr: - **دور الفئة** — الوظيفة المسندة إلى فئة (وجهة أو روتين أو عرضي / موسمي أو مريح)، والتي تحدد المساحة واتساع الفرز وموقف التسعير.

segments.src: - **GMROI** — Gross margin return on inventory investment: gross margin dollars divided by average inventory at cost; the profit earned per dollar tied up in stock.
segments.tr: - **GMROI** — إجمالي هامش العائد على الاستثمار في المخزون: دولارات الهامش الإجمالي مقسومة على متوسط الجرد بسعر التكلفة؛ الربح الذي حققته لكل دولار محتفظ به في المخزون.

segments.src: - **Inventory turnover** — How many times a year inventory is sold and replaced (COGS ÷ average inventory at cost); higher turns free up cash and reduce markdown risk.
segments.tr: - **معدل دوران الجرد** — كم مرة في السنة يتم بيع المخزون واستبداله (COGS ÷ متوسط الجرد بسعر التكلفة)؛ الدورات الأعلى تحرر النقد وتقلل من خطر الخصم.

segments.src: - **EDLP vs. high–low** — Two pricing strategies: consistently low everyday prices, versus a higher base price punctuated by frequent deep promotions.
segments.tr: - **EDLP مقابل high-low** — استراتيجيتان للتسعير: أسعار منخفضة يومية متسقة، مقابل سعر أساسي أعلى يتخللها عروض ترويجية عميقة متكررة.
