segments.tr: هذا يصف التسعير high-low؛ EDLP يتجنب عن قصد دورة promo لصالح الأسعار المستقرة والمتوقعة.

segments.src: Milk and eggs are classic key value items whose prices shoppers actually remember, so they're priced to build traffic and price image, with margin recovered elsewhere in the basket.*
segments.tr: الحليب والبيض عناصر قيمة رئيسية كلاسيكية تتذكر أسعارها المتسوقون فعلياً، لذا يتم تسعيرها لبناء حركة المرور وصورة السعر، مع استرجاع الهامش في مكان آخر من السلة.*

fr.title: [Commerce de détail 101 #9] Chaque rayon est une petite entreprise, et il a son propre P&L

segments.src: > One-line summary: Advanced merchandising means running each category like a standalone business — giving it a job to do, measuring the return on the cash parked in its inventory, and setting prices that protect both margin and price image.
segments.tr: > Résumé en une ligne : Le marchandisage avancé consiste à gérer chaque catégorie comme une entreprise autonome — lui assigner une mission, mesurer le retour sur la trésorerie immobilisée dans son inventaire, et fixer les prix qui protègent à la fois la marge et l'image de prix.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Le concept d'aujourd'hui

segments.src: Last time we met the person who picked everything on the shelf six months before you walked in.
segments.tr: La dernière fois, nous avons rencontré la personne qui a sélectionné tout ce qui est sur l'étagère six mois avant votre arrivée.

segments.src: Today: how they actually decide.
segments.tr: Aujourd'hui : comment ils décident réellement.

segments.src: Three levers do most of the work.
segments.tr: Trois leviers font la majeure partie du travail.

segments.src: Category management — the aisle has a job.**
segments.tr: Gestion des catégories — le rayon a une mission.**

segments.src: Instead of buying product by product, retailers group items the way shoppers think about them ("oral care," not "tubes we get from Colgate") and manage that group as a business unit.
segments.tr: Au lieu d'acheter produit par produit, les détaillants regroupent les articles comme les clients y pensent (« soins bucco-dentaires », pas « les tubes que nous obtenons de Colgate ») et gèrent ce groupe comme une unité commerciale.

segments.src: The framework, popularized in the 1990s through the industry's Efficient Consumer Response push, starts by assigning each category a **role**:
segments.tr: Le cadre, popularisé dans les années 1990 par le mouvement Efficient Consumer Response de l'industrie, commence par assigner à chaque catégorie un **rôle** :

segments.src: - **Destination** — a reason to choose this store over the one down the road. Deep assortment, sharp prices, lots of space.
segments.tr: - **Destination** — une raison de choisir ce magasin plutôt que celui d'à côté. Assortiment profond, prix compétitifs, beaucoup d'espace.

segments.src: - **Routine** — the everyday workhorse that builds the basket and carries margin. Most of the store lives here.
segments.tr: - **Routine** — le cheval de trait quotidien qui construit le panier et porte la marge. La plupart du magasin vit ici.

segments.src: - **Occasional / seasonal** — grilling supplies in June, school glue in August.
segments.tr: - **Occasionnel / saisonnier** — fournitures de grillades en juin, colle scolaire en août.

segments.src: - **Convenience** — you didn't come for it, but it's there. Fewer options, healthier margins.
segments.tr: - **Commodité** — vous n'êtes pas venu pour ça, mais c'est là. Moins d'options, des marges plus saines.

segments.src: The role drives everything downstream: how many SKUs, how much shelf, how aggressive the price, how much promo money.
segments.tr: Le rôle détermine tout en aval : combien de SKU, combien d'étagère, à quel point le prix est agressif, combien d'argent de promotion.

segments.src: A destination category and a convenience category get opposite treatment on purpose.
segments.tr: Une catégorie de destination et une catégorie de commodité reçoivent un traitement opposé intentionnellement.

segments.src: One wrinkle worth knowing: retailers often name a **category captain** — usually the biggest supplier — to help build the plan, since that vendor has the best data.
segments.tr: Un détail qui vaut la peine d'être connu : les détaillants nomment souvent un **capitaine de catégorie** — généralement le plus grand fournisseur — pour aider à construire le plan, car ce fournisseur a les meilleures données.

segments.src: It's efficient and it's a conflict of interest at the same time, which is why captains' recommendations get audited and why the practice draws antitrust attention.
segments.tr: C'est efficace et c'est un conflit d'intérêts en même temps, ce qui explique pourquoi les recommandations des capitaines sont auditées et pourquoi la pratique attire l'attention de la concurrence.

segments.src: Inventory management — the shelf is a bank account.**
segments.tr: Gestion des stocks — l'étagère est un compte bancaire.**

segments.src: Every unit on that shelf is cash the retailer can't use for anything else.
segments.tr: Chaque unité sur cette étagère est de la trésorerie que le détaillant ne peut utiliser pour rien d'autre.

segments.src: So the question isn't "did it sell?"
segments.tr: Donc la question n'est pas « s'est-il vendu ? »

segments.src: but "what did it earn per dollar tied up?"
segments.tr: mais « combien a-t-il gagné par dollar immobilisé ? »

segments.src: Two numbers carry the load:
segments.tr: Deux chiffres portent le poids :

segments.src: inventory turnover = cost of goods sold / average inventory at cost
segments.tr: inventory turnover = cost of goods sold / average inventory at cost

segments.src: GMROI = gross margin dollars / average inventory at cost
segments.tr: GMROI = gross margin dollars / average inventory at cost

segments.src: weeks of supply = 52 / annual turns
segments.tr: weeks of supply = 52 / annual turns

segments.src: GMROI of 2.5 means the category returned $2.50 of gross margin for every $1 invested in inventory.
segments.tr: Un GMROI de 2,5 signifie que la catégorie a retourné 2,50 $ de marge brute pour chaque 1 $ investi en stock.

segments.src: This is why a low-margin item that turns 20 times a year can beat a high-margin item that turns twice — and why buyers argue about turns more than about markup.
segments.tr: C'est pourquoi un article à faible marge qui tourne 20 fois par an peut surpasser un article à marge élevée qui tourne deux fois — et pourquoi les acheteurs discutent plus des rotations que de la majoration.

segments.src: The counterweight is service level.
segments.tr: Le contrepoids est le niveau de service.

segments.src: Order less and you free cash but risk an out-of-stock, which costs the sale and sometimes the trip.
segments.tr: Commandez moins et vous libérez de la trésorerie mais risquez une rupture de stock, ce qui coûte la vente et parfois le voyage.

segments.src: So teams hold **safety stock** and set a reorder point:
segments.tr: Donc les équipes maintiennent un **stock de sécurité** et fixent un point de réapprovisionnement :

segments.src: reorder point = expected demand during lead time + safety stock
segments.tr: reorder point = expected demand during lead time + safety stock

segments.src: Then there's leakage.
segments.tr: Ensuite, il y a les fuites.

segments.src: **Shrink** — theft, damage, spoilage, paperwork errors — has run around 1.5% of sales in recent National Retail Federation security surveys.
segments.tr: **La démarque** — vol, dommages, dégâts, erreurs administratives — s'est située autour de 1,5 % des ventes dans les récentes enquêtes de sécurité de la National Retail Federation.

segments.src: On thin retail margins, that's not rounding.
segments.tr: Avec des marges commerciales minces, ce n'est pas un arrondi.

segments.src: Pricing — margin and image, at the same time.**
segments.tr: Tarification — marge et image, en même temps.**

segments.src: The arithmetic is easy:
segments.tr: L'arithmétique est simple :

segments.src: retail price = cost / (1 - target margin %)
segments.tr: retail price = cost / (1 - target margin %)

segments.src: "Keystone" markup just means doubling cost: a $5 item retails at $10, a 50% margin.
segments.tr: La majoration « Keystone » signifie simplement doubler le coût : un article de 5 $ se vend au détail à 10 $, une marge de 50 %.

segments.src: The strategy is the hard part, and it splits two ways.
segments.tr: La stratégie est la partie difficile, et elle se divise en deux façons.

segments.src: **EDLP** (everyday low price) keeps prices flat and predictable — Walmart, Costco, Aldi.
segments.tr: **EDLP** (prix bas quotidiens) maintient les prix stables et prévisibles — Walmart, Costco, Aldi.

segments.src: **High–low** runs a base price plus frequent, deep promotions, often gated behind a loyalty card — most conventional supermarkets and department stores.
segments.tr: **Haut–bas** utilise un prix de base plus des promotions fréquentes et profondes, souvent limitées par une carte de fidélité — la plupart des supermarchés et magasins de département conventionnels.

segments.src: EDLP smooths demand and cuts labor spent re-ticketing; high–low creates urgency and pulls in deal-sensitive shoppers, at the cost of training people to wait for the sale.
segments.tr: EDLP lisse la demande et réduit le travail de ré-étiquetage ; haut–bas crée de l'urgence et attire les clients sensibles aux bonnes affaires, au prix de former les gens à attendre la vente.

segments.src: Either way, no one prices 40,000 items with equal care.
segments.tr: De toute façon, personne ne fixe le prix de 40 000 articles avec un soin égal.

segments.src: Shoppers only remember a few dozen **key value items** — milk, eggs, bananas, a 12-pack of soda — and those set the store's price image.
segments.tr: Les clients se souviennent seulement de quelques douzaines d'**articles clés** — lait, œufs, bananes, un pack de 12 sodas — et ceux-ci fixent l'image de prix du magasin.

segments.src: Those get priced sharply, sometimes at or below cost as a **loss leader**, and the margin is recovered on the rest of the basket.
segments.tr: Ceux-ci sont fixés à prix compétitif, parfois au coût ou en dessous comme un **produit d'appel**, et la marge est récupérée sur le reste du panier.

segments.src: (Loss leaders are generally legal, though a number of states have minimum-markup laws, usually covering gas, alcohol, or tobacco.)
segments.tr: (Les produits d'appel sont généralement légaux, bien qu'un certain nombre d'États aient des lois de majoration minimale, couvrant généralement l'essence, l'alcool ou le tabac.)

segments.src: And when inventory ages, **markdowns** are the release valve: a planned cadence of cuts that converts stale stock back into cash before it's worth nothing.
segments.tr: Et lorsque l'inventaire vieillit, les **réductions** sont la soupape de décharge : une cadence planifiée de réductions qui convertit le stock obsolète en trésorerie avant qu'il ne vaille plus rien.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Dans la vie quotidienne

segments.src: Sunday morning, a Kroger on the north side of Columbus.
segments.tr: Dimanche matin, un Kroger au nord de Columbus.

segments.src: Your cart: a gallon of milk, cereal, toothpaste, tortilla chips, a rotisserie chicken.
segments.tr: Votre panier : un gallon de lait, des céréales, du dentifrice, des tortillas chips, un poulet rôti.

segments.src: The milk is a key value item.
segments.tr: Le lait est un article clé.

segments.src: It's priced within pennies of the Meijer two miles away because management assumes you know roughly what milk costs.
segments.tr: Il est fixé à quelques cents du Meijer à deux miles de là, car la direction suppose que vous savez à peu près quel est le coût du lait.

segments.src: The rotisserie chicken is close to a loss leader — cooked from a bird that would've been marked down anyway, priced to get you through the door on the one trip where you might also buy a $30 cut of steak.
segments.tr: Le poulet rôti est proche d'un produit d'appel — cuit à partir d'un oiseau qui aurait de toute façon été réduit, fixé pour vous faire entrer par la porte sur le seul voyage où vous pourriez aussi acheter une côte de bifteck de 30 $.

segments.src: Costco has famously held its chicken at $4.99 for years for exactly this reason.
segments.tr: Costco a maintenu son poulet à 4,99 $ pendant des années pour exactement cette raison.

segments.src: The toothpaste tells the category story.
segments.tr: Le dentifrice raconte l'histoire de la catégorie.

segments.src: Oral care is a routine category here, so you get maybe 40 SKUs, not 90, and the shelf runs a familiar pattern: a national brand at eye level, the Kroger store brand right beside it at a lower price and a higher margin, and the $9 whitening kit on the top shelf where it turns slowly but earns well when it does.
segments.tr: Les soins bucco-dentaires sont une catégorie de routine ici, donc vous obtenez peut-être 40 SKU, pas 90, et l'étagère suit un modèle familier : une marque nationale au niveau des yeux, la marque maison Kroger juste à côté à un prix inférieur et une marge plus élevée, et le kit blanchissant de 9 $ sur l'étagère supérieure où il tourne lentement mais gagne bien quand il le fait.

segments.src: The chips are near the front — high turns, decent margin, impulse-friendly placement.
segments.tr: Les chips sont près de l'avant — rotations élevées, marge décente, placement impulsif.

segments.src: And the endcap you walked past with the seasonal cooler display?
segments.tr: Et le présentoir en bout de rayon que vous avez dépassé avec l'écran de refroidisseur saisonnier ?

segments.src: That's an occasional category, bought in a single seasonal buy, with a markdown schedule already written for late August.
segments.tr: C'est une catégorie occasionnelle, achetée en un seul achat saisonnier, avec un calendrier de réduction déjà écrit pour fin août.

segments.src: Nobody will scramble when it stops selling.
segments.tr: Personne ne s'affolera quand il arrêtera de se vendre.

segments.src: That was the plan in April.
segments.tr: C'était le plan en avril.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Récapitulatif en trois lignes

segments.src: 1. Category management treats each group of products as a business with an assigned role — destination, routine, occasional, or convenience — and that role drives assortment, space, and price aggressiveness.
segments.tr: 1. La gestion des catégories traite chaque groupe de produits comme une entreprise avec un rôle assigné — destination, routine, occasionnel ou commodité — et ce rôle détermine l'assortiment, l'espace et l'agressivité des prix.

segments.src: 2. Inventory is capital, so retailers judge it by turns and GMROI (gross margin per dollar invested), balancing that against the cost of being out of stock.
segments.tr: 2. L'inventaire est du capital, donc les détaillants le jugent par les rotations et le GMROI (marge brute par dollar investi), équilibrant cela avec le coût d'une rupture de stock.

segments.src: 3. Pricing is a portfolio: sharp on the handful of key value items that shape price image, and recovered across everything else — under either an EDLP or a high–low strategy.
segments.tr: 3. La tarification est un portefeuille : compétitif sur la poignée d'articles clés qui façonnent l'image de prix, et récupérée sur tout le reste — selon une stratégie EDLP ou haut–bas.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Termes d'aujourd'hui

segments.src: - **Category management** — Managing a group of related products as a single business unit with its own role, strategy, and scorecard, rather than item by item.
segments.tr: - **Gestion des catégories** — Gérer un groupe de produits connexes comme une unité commerciale unique avec son propre rôle, stratégie et tableau de bord, plutôt que article par article.

segments.src: - **Category role** — The job assigned to a category (destination, routine, occasional/seasonal, convenience), which determines its space, assortment breadth, and pricing posture.
segments.tr: - **Rôle de catégorie** — La mission assignée à une catégorie (destination, routine, occasionnel/saisonnier, commodité), qui détermine son espace, sa profondeur d'assortiment et sa position tarifaire.

segments.src: - **GMROI** — Gross margin return on inventory investment: gross margin dollars divided by average inventory at cost; the profit earned per dollar tied up in stock.
segments.tr: - **GMROI** — Rendement de la marge brute sur l'investissement en stocks : dollars de marge brute divisés par l'inventaire moyen au coût ; le bénéfice gagné par dollar immobilisé en stock.

segments.src: - **Inventory turnover** — How many times a year inventory is sold and replaced (COGS ÷ average inventory at cost); higher turns free up cash and reduce markdown risk.
segments.tr: - **Rotation des stocks** — Combien de fois par an l'inventaire est vendu et remplacé (COGS ÷ inventaire moyen au coût) ; les rotations plus élevées libèrent de la trésorerie et réduisent le risque de réduction.

segments.src: - **EDLP vs. high–low** — Two pricing strategies: consistently low everyday prices, versus a higher base price punctuated by frequent deep promotions.
segments.tr: - **EDLP vs. haut–bas** — Deux stratégies tarifaires : prix quotidiens constamment bas, par rapport à un prix de base plus élevé ponctué par des promotions profondes fréquentes.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap

segments.src: 1. Category management treats each group of products as a business with an assigned role — destination, routine, occasional, or convenience — and that role drives assortment, space, and price aggressiveness.

segments.src: 2. Inventory is capital, so retailers judge it by turns and GMROI (gross margin per dollar invested), balancing that against the cost of being out of stock.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Termos de Hoje

segments.src: - **Category management** — Managing a group of related products as a single business unit with its own role, strategy, and scorecard, rather than item by item.
segments.tr: - **Gerenciamento de categoria** — Gerenciar um grupo de produtos relacionados como uma única unidade de negócios com seu próprio papel, estratégia e placar, em vez de item por item.

segments.src: - **Category role** — The job assigned to a category (destination, routine, occasional/seasonal, convenience), which determines its space, assortment breadth, and pricing posture.
segments.tr: - **Papel da categoria** — O trabalho atribuído a uma categoria (destino, rotina, ocasional/sazonal, conveniência), que determina seu espaço, amplitude de sortimento e postura de preço.

segments.src: - **GMROI** — Gross margin return on inventory investment: gross margin dollars divided by average inventory at cost; the profit earned per dollar tied up in stock.
segments.tr: - **GMROI** — Retorno de margem bruta sobre investimento em inventário: dólares de margem bruta divididos pelo inventário médio ao custo; o lucro obtido por dólar investido em estoque.

segments.src: - **Inventory turnover** — How many times a year inventory is sold and replaced (COGS ÷ average inventory at cost); higher turns free up cash and reduce markdown risk.
segments.tr: - **Giro de inventário** — Quantas vezes por ano o inventário é vendido e substituído (COGS ÷ inventário médio ao custo); giros mais altos liberam dinheiro e reduzem risco de redução de preço.

segments.src: - **EDLP vs. high–low** — Two pricing strategies: consistently low everyday prices, versus a higher base price punctuated by frequent deep promotions.
segments.tr: - **EDLP vs. alto-baixo** — Duas estratégias de precificação: preços baixos consistentes todos os dias, versus um preço base mais alto pontuado por promoções profundas frequentes.

in.title: [Retailing 101 #9] Setiap Lorong adalah Bisnis Kecil, dan Punya P&L-nya Sendiri

segments.src: > One-line summary: Advanced merchandising means running each category like a standalone business — giving it a job to do, measuring the return on the cash parked in its inventory, and setting prices that protect both margin and price image.
segments.tr: > Ringkasan satu baris: Merchandising canggih berarti menjalankan setiap kategori seperti bisnis mandiri — memberinya pekerjaan untuk dilakukan, mengukur pengembalian kas yang tertanam dalam inventorinya, dan menetapkan harga yang melindungi margin dan citra harga.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Konsep Hari Ini

segments.src: Last time we met the person who picked everything on the shelf six months before you walked in.
segments.tr: Terakhir kali kami bertemu orang yang memilih semua yang ada di rak enam bulan sebelum Anda masuk.

segments.src: Today: how they actually decide.
segments.tr: Hari ini: bagaimana mereka benar-benar memutuskan.

segments.src: Three levers do most of the work.
segments.tr: Tiga tuas melakukan sebagian besar pekerjaan.

segments.src: Category management — the aisle has a job.**
segments.tr: Manajemen kategori — lorong memiliki pekerjaan.**

segments.src: Instead of buying product by product, retailers group items the way shoppers think about them ("oral care," not "tubes we get from Colgate") and manage that group as a business unit.
segments.tr: Alih-alih membeli produk demi produk, pengecer mengelompokkan barang dengan cara pembeli memikirkannya ("perawatan mulut," bukan "tabung yang kami dapatkan dari Colgate") dan mengelola kelompok tersebut sebagai unit bisnis.

segments.src: The framework, popularized in the 1990s through the industry's Efficient Consumer Response push, starts by assigning each category a **role**:
segments.tr: Kerangka kerja, yang dipopulerkan pada tahun 1990-an melalui dorongan Efficient Consumer Response industri, dimulai dengan menetapkan **peran** untuk setiap kategori:

segments.src: - **Destination** — a reason to choose this store over the one down the road. Deep assortment, sharp prices, lots of space.
segments.tr: - **Tujuan** — alasan memilih toko ini daripada yang di jalan. Penawaran mendalam, harga tajam, banyak tempat.

segments.src: - **Routine** — the everyday workhorse that builds the basket and carries margin. Most of the store lives here.
segments.tr: - **Rutin** — kuda kerja sehari-hari yang membangun keranjang dan membawa margin. Sebagian besar toko hidup di sini.

segments.src: - **Occasional / seasonal** — grilling supplies in June, school glue in August.
segments.tr: - **Sesekali/musiman** — perlengkapan pemanggang di Juni, lem sekolah di Agustus.

segments.src: - **Convenience** — you didn't come for it, but it's there. Fewer options, healthier margins.
segments.tr: - **Kenyamanan** — Anda tidak datang untuk itu, tetapi ada di sana. Lebih sedikit pilihan, margin yang lebih sehat.

segments.src: The role drives everything downstream: how many SKUs, how much shelf, how aggressive the price, how much promo money.
segments.tr: Peran mendorong segalanya: berapa banyak SKU, berapa banyak rak, seberapa agresif harganya, berapa banyak uang promo.

segments.src: A destination category and a convenience category get opposite treatment on purpose.
segments.tr: Kategori tujuan dan kategori kenyamanan mendapat perlakuan yang berlawanan dengan sengaja.

segments.src: One wrinkle worth knowing: retailers often name a **category captain** — usually the biggest supplier — to help build the plan, since that vendor has the best data.
segments.tr: Satu kerutan yang patut diketahui: pengecer sering menamakan **kapten kategori** — biasanya pemasok terbesar — untuk membantu membangun rencana, karena vendor itu memiliki data terbaik.

segments.src: It's efficient and it's a conflict of interest at the same time, which is why captains' recommendations get audited and why the practice draws antitrust attention.
segments.tr: Ini efisien dan merupakan konflik kepentingan pada saat yang bersamaan, itulah mengapa rekomendasi kapten diaudit dan mengapa praktik ini menarik perhatian antitrust.

segments.src: Inventory management — the shelf is a bank account.**
segments.tr: Manajemen inventori — rak adalah rekening bank.**

segments.src: Every unit on that shelf is cash the retailer can't use for anything else.
segments.tr: Setiap unit di rak itu adalah uang tunai yang tidak dapat digunakan pengecer untuk hal lain.

segments.src: So the question isn't "did it sell?"
segments.tr: Jadi pertanyaannya bukan "apakah itu terjual?"

segments.src: but "what did it earn per dollar tied up?"
segments.tr: tetapi "apa yang itu hasilkan per dolar yang terikat?"

segments.src: Two numbers carry the load:
segments.tr: Dua angka membawa beban:

segments.src: inventory turnover = cost of goods sold / average inventory at cost
segments.tr: inventory turnover = cost of goods sold / average inventory at cost

segments.src: GMROI = gross margin dollars / average inventory at cost
segments.tr: GMROI = gross margin dollars / average inventory at cost

segments.src: weeks of supply = 52 / annual turns
segments.tr: weeks of supply = 52 / annual turns

segments.src: GMROI of 2.5 means the category returned $2.50 of gross margin for every $1 invested in inventory.
segments.tr: GMROI 2,5 berarti kategori mengembalikan $2,50 margin kotor untuk setiap $1 yang diinvestasikan dalam inventori.

segments.src: This is why a low-margin item that turns 20 times a year can beat a high-margin item that turns twice — and why buyers argue about turns more than about markup.
segments.tr: Inilah mengapa item margin rendah yang berputar 20 kali setahun dapat mengalahkan item margin tinggi yang berputar dua kali — dan mengapa pembeli berdebat tentang turns lebih banyak daripada tentang markup.

segments.src: The counterweight is service level.
segments.tr: Penyeimbang adalah tingkat layanan.

segments.src: Order less and you free cash but risk an out-of-stock, which costs the sale and sometimes the trip.
segments.tr: Pesan lebih sedikit dan Anda membebaskan uang tunai tetapi risiko kehabisan stok, yang menghabiskan penjualan dan kadang-kadang perjalanan.

segments.src: So teams hold **safety stock** and set a reorder point:
segments.tr: Jadi tim menyimpan **stok keselamatan** dan menetapkan titik pemesanan ulang:

segments.src: reorder point = expected demand during lead time + safety stock
segments.tr: reorder point = expected demand during lead time + safety stock

segments.src: Then there's leakage.
segments.tr: Kemudian ada kebocoran.

segments.src: **Shrink** — theft, damage, spoilage, paperwork errors — has run around 1.5% of sales in recent National Retail Federation security surveys.
segments.tr: **Shrink** — pencurian, kerusakan, pembusukan, kesalahan dokumen — telah berkisar sekitar 1,5% penjualan dalam survei keamanan National Retail Federation terbaru.

segments.src: On thin retail margins, that's not rounding.
segments.tr: Dengan margin ritel tipis, itu bukan pembulatan.

segments.src: Pricing — margin and image, at the same time.**
segments.tr: Penetapan harga — margin dan citra, pada saat yang bersamaan.**

segments.src: The arithmetic is easy:
segments.tr: Aritmatikanya mudah:

segments.src: retail price = cost / (1 - target margin %)
segments.tr: retail price = cost / (1 - target margin %)

segments.src: "Keystone" markup just means doubling cost: a $5 item retails at $10, a 50% margin.
segments.tr: Markup "Keystone" hanya berarti menggandakan biaya: item $5 dijual dengan harga $10, margin 50%.

segments.src: The strategy is the hard part, and it splits two ways.
segments.tr: Strategi adalah bagian yang sulit, dan itu terbagi dua cara.

segments.src: **EDLP** (everyday low price) keeps prices flat and predictable — Walmart, Costco, Aldi.
segments.tr: **EDLP** (harga rendah setiap hari) menjaga harga tetap dan dapat diprediksi — Walmart, Costco, Aldi.

segments.src: **High–low** runs a base price plus frequent, deep promotions, often gated behind a loyalty card — most conventional supermarkets and department stores.
segments.tr: **High–low** menjalankan harga dasar ditambah promosi yang sering dan mendalam, sering dikunci di balik kartu loyalitas — sebagian besar supermarket dan toko department konvensional.

segments.src: EDLP smooths demand and cuts labor spent re-ticketing; high–low creates urgency and pulls in deal-sensitive shoppers, at the cost of training people to wait for the sale.
segments.tr: EDLP meratakan permintaan dan mengurangi tenaga kerja yang dihabiskan untuk re-ticketing; high–low menciptakan urgensi dan menarik pembeli yang sensitif terhadap penawaran, dengan biaya melatih orang menunggu penjualan.

segments.src: Either way, no one prices 40,000 items with equal care.
segments.tr: Bagaimanapun, tidak ada yang menentukan harga 40.000 barang dengan perhatian yang sama.

segments.src: Shoppers only remember a few dozen **key value items** — milk, eggs, bananas, a 12-pack of soda — and those set the store's price image.
segments.tr: Pembeli hanya mengingat beberapa lusin **item nilai kunci** — susu, telur, pisang, paket 12 soda — dan itu menetapkan citra harga toko.

segments.src: Those get priced sharply, sometimes at or below cost as a **loss leader**, and the margin is recovered on the rest of the basket.
segments.tr: Mereka dihargai dengan tajam, kadang-kadang pada atau di bawah biaya sebagai **pemimpin kerugian**, dan margin dipulihkan di sisa keranjang.

segments.src: (Loss leaders are generally legal, though a number of states have minimum-markup laws, usually covering gas, alcohol, or tobacco.)
segments.tr: (Pemimpin kerugian umumnya legal, meskipun sejumlah negara memiliki undang-undang markup minimum, biasanya mencakup gas, alkohol, atau tembakau.)

segments.src: And when inventory ages, **markdowns** are the release valve: a planned cadence of cuts that converts stale stock back into cash before it's worth nothing.
segments.tr: Dan ketika inventori menua, **markdowns** adalah katup pelepas: irama terencana dari potongan yang mengubah stok basi kembali menjadi uang tunai sebelum tidak bernilai.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Istilah Hari Ini

segments.src: - **Category management** — Managing a group of related products as a single business unit with its own role, strategy, and scorecard, rather than item by item.
segments.tr: - **Manajemen kategori** — Mengelola kelompok produk terkait sebagai unit bisnis tunggal dengan peran, strategi, dan kartu skornya sendiri, bukan item demi item.

segments.src: - **Category role** — The job assigned to a category (destination, routine, occasional/seasonal, convenience), which determines its space, assortment breadth, and pricing posture.
segments.tr: - **Peran kategori** — Pekerjaan yang ditugaskan ke kategori (tujuan, rutin, sesekali/musiman, kenyamanan), yang menentukan ruang, lebar penawaran, dan postur penetapan harganya.

segments.src: - **GMROI** — Gross margin return on inventory investment: gross margin dollars divided by average inventory at cost; the profit earned per dollar tied up in stock.
segments.tr: - **GMROI** — Pengembalian margin kotor pada investasi inventori: dolar margin kotor dibagi dengan inventori rata-rata dengan biaya; keuntungan yang diperoleh per dolar yang terikat dalam stok.

segments.src: - **Inventory turnover** — How many times a year inventory is sold and replaced (COGS ÷ average inventory at cost); higher turns free up cash and reduce markdown risk.
segments.tr: - **Perputaran inventori** — Berapa kali setahun inventori dijual dan diganti (COGS ÷ inventori rata-rata dengan biaya); putaran lebih tinggi membebaskan uang tunai dan mengurangi risiko markdown.

segments.src: - **EDLP vs. high–low** — Two pricing strategies: consistently low everyday prices, versus a higher base price punctuated by frequent deep promotions.
segments.tr: - **EDLP vs. high–low** — Dua strategi penetapan harga: harga sehari-hari yang secara konsisten rendah, versus harga dasar yang lebih tinggi yang ditandai dengan promosi mendalam yang sering.

ja.title: [Retailing 101 #9] 小売の各セクション（通路）は独立した小規模ビジネス — 独自の損益計算書を持つ

segments.src: > One-line summary: Advanced merchandising means running each category like a standalone business — giving it a job to do, measuring the return on the cash parked in its inventory, and setting prices that protect both margin and price image.
segments.tr: > 一行要約：高度なマーチャンダイジングとは、各カテゴリーを独立したビジネスのように運営すること—各カテゴリーに役割を与え、棚卸資産に投入された現金のリターンを測定し、利益率と価格イメージの両方を守る価格を設定することです。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日のコンセプト

segments.src: Last time we met the person who picked everything on the shelf six months before you walked in.
segments.tr: 前回、あなたが来店する6ヶ月前に棚の商品をすべて選んだ人に会いました。

segments.src: Today: how they actually decide.
segments.tr: 今回：彼らが実際にどのように決定するか。

segments.src: Three levers do most of the work.
segments.tr: 3つのレバーがほとんどの仕事を担っています。

segments.src: Category management — the aisle has a job.**
segments.tr: カテゴリー管理—通路は役割を持っています。**

segments.src: Instead of buying product by product, retailers group items the way shoppers think about them ("oral care," not "tubes we get from Colgate") and manage that group as a business unit.
segments.tr: 小売業者は、商品を1つずつ購入するのではなく、買い物客が考える方法でアイテムをグループ化し（「コルゲートから得たチューブ」ではなく「オーラルケア」）、そのグループをビジネスユニットとして管理します。

segments.src: The framework, popularized in the 1990s through the industry's Efficient Consumer Response push, starts by assigning each category a **role**:
segments.tr: 1990年代に業界の効率的消費者反応（ECR）推進を通じて普及したフレームワークは、各カテゴリーに**役割**を割り当てることから始まります：

segments.src: - **Destination** — a reason to choose this store over the one down the road. Deep assortment, sharp prices, lots of space.
segments.tr: - **目的地型**—近所の店ではなくこの店を選ぶ理由。深い品揃え、低価格、スペースが豊富。

segments.src: - **Routine** — the everyday workhorse that builds the basket and carries margin. Most of the store lives here.
segments.tr: - **ルーチン型**—買い物かごを増やし、利益をもたらす日常的な主力商品。店舗のほとんどがここに集中しています。

segments.src: - **Occasional / seasonal** — grilling supplies in June, school glue in August.
segments.tr: - **たまに/季節型**—6月のグリル用品、8月の学校用接着剤。

segments.src: - **Convenience** — you didn't come for it, but it's there. Fewer options, healthier margins.
segments.tr: - **利便型**—あなたはそれを目的に来たわけではありませんが、そこにあります。選択肢が少ない、利益率がより高い。

segments.src: The role drives everything downstream: how many SKUs, how much shelf, how aggressive the price, how much promo money.
segments.tr: その役割は、SKU数、棚スペース、価格の積極性、プロモーション費用の額など、すべての後続決定を左右します。

segments.src: A destination category and a convenience category get opposite treatment on purpose.
segments.tr: 目的地型カテゴリーと利便型カテゴリーは、意図的に正反対の扱いを受けます。

segments.src: One wrinkle worth knowing: retailers often name a **category captain** — usually the biggest supplier — to help build the plan, since that vendor has the best data.
segments.tr: 知っておく価値のあるもう1つの点：小売業者は、そのベンダーが最高のデータを持っているため、計画構築を支援するために**カテゴリーキャプテン**（通常は最大の供給業者）を指名することがよくあります。

segments.src: It's efficient and it's a conflict of interest at the same time, which is why captains' recommendations get audited and why the practice draws antitrust attention.
segments.tr: それは効率的であり、同時に利益相反であり、それが理由で、キャプテンの推奨事項が監査され、この慣行が反トラスト法の注目を集めるのです。

segments.src: Inventory management — the shelf is a bank account.**
segments.tr: 在庫管理—棚は銀行口座です。**

segments.src: Every unit on that shelf is cash the retailer can't use for anything else.
segments.tr: その棚のすべてのユニットは、小売業者が他に使用できない現金です。

segments.src: So the question isn't "did it sell?"
segments.tr: したがって、質問は「それは売れたか？」ではありません。

segments.src: but "what did it earn per dollar tied up?"
segments.tr: しかし「投入された1ドルあたりいくら稼いだか？」です。

segments.src: Two numbers carry the load:
segments.tr: 2つの数字が重要な役割を担っています：

segments.src: inventory turnover = cost of goods sold / average inventory at cost
segments.tr: inventory turnover = cost of goods sold / average inventory at cost

segments.src: GMROI = gross margin dollars / average inventory at cost
segments.tr: GMROI = gross margin dollars / average inventory at cost

segments.src: weeks of supply = 52 / annual turns
segments.tr: weeks of supply = 52 / annual turns

segments.src: GMROI of 2.5 means the category returned $2.50 of gross margin for every $1 invested in inventory.
segments.tr: 2.5のGMROIは、カテゴリーが在庫に投入された1ドルあたり2.50ドルの粗利益をもたらしたことを意味します。

segments.src: This is why a low-margin item that turns 20 times a year can beat a high-margin item that turns twice — and why buyers argue about turns more than about markup.
segments.tr: これが、年20回転する低利益率品が年2回転する高利益率品に勝つ理由であり、購買者がマークアップについてより回転について議論する理由です。

segments.src: The counterweight is service level.
segments.tr: 対する要素は、サービスレベルです。

segments.src: Order less and you free cash but risk an out-of-stock, which costs the sale and sometimes the trip.
segments.tr: 注文を減らすと、現金が解放されますが、在庫切れのリスクが生じ、販売と時には購買旅程全体の喪失につながります。

segments.src: So teams hold **safety stock** and set a reorder point:
segments.tr: したがって、チームは**安全在庫**を保有し、再注文点を設定します：

segments.src: reorder point = expected demand during lead time + safety stock
segments.tr: reorder point = expected demand during lead time + safety stock

segments.src: Then there's leakage.
segments.tr: その後、漏れがあります。

segments.src: **Shrink** — theft, damage, spoilage, paperwork errors — has run around 1.5% of sales in recent National Retail Federation security surveys.
segments.tr: **シュリンク**—盗難、破損、腐敗、事務エラー—最近の全米小売連盟セキュリティ調査で売上の約1.5%に達しています。

segments.src: On thin retail margins, that's not rounding.
segments.tr: 小売業の薄い利益率では、これは軽視できない数字です。

segments.src: Pricing — margin and image, at the same time.**
segments.tr: 価格設定—利益率と価格イメージ、同時に。**

segments.src: The arithmetic is easy:
segments.tr: 計算は簡単です：

segments.src: retail price = cost / (1 - target margin %)
segments.tr: retail price = cost / (1 - target margin %)

segments.src: "Keystone" markup just means doubling cost: a $5 item retails at $10, a 50% margin.
segments.tr: 「キーストーン」マークアップは、単にコストを2倍にすることを意味します：5ドルの商品は10ドルで小売され、50％の利益率です。

segments.src: The strategy is the hard part, and it splits two ways.
segments.tr: 戦略が難しい部分であり、2つの方法に分かれます。

segments.src: **EDLP** (everyday low price) keeps prices flat and predictable — Walmart, Costco, Aldi.
segments.tr: **EDLP**（日々の低価格）は価格を平坦で予測可能に保つ—ウォルマート、コストコ、アルディ。

segments.src: **High–low** runs a base price plus frequent, deep promotions, often gated behind a loyalty card — most conventional supermarkets and department stores.
segments.tr: **ハイロー戦略**は基本価格に加えて、頻繁な大幅プロモーション（多くの場合、ロイヤルティカードの後ろにゲートがある）を実施します—ほとんどの従来型スーパーマーケットと百貨店。

segments.src: EDLP smooths demand and cuts labor spent re-ticketing; high–low creates urgency and pulls in deal-sensitive shoppers, at the cost of training people to wait for the sale.
segments.tr: EDLPは需要を平準化し、価格タグの貼り直しに費やす労働を削減します；ハイロー戦略は緊迫感を生み出し、セール待機型の顧客を引き寄せます。その代わり、人々をセール待ちに慣らすコストがあります。

segments.src: Either way, no one prices 40,000 items with equal care.
segments.tr: いずれにせよ、誰も40,000個の品目を同等の注意で価格設定することはありません。

segments.src: Shoppers only remember a few dozen **key value items** — milk, eggs, bananas, a 12-pack of soda — and those set the store's price image.
segments.tr: 買い物客は数十の**主要値引き商品**—牛乳、卵、バナナ、12パック炭酸飲料—しか記憶せず、これらが店舗の価格イメージを設定します。

segments.src: Those get priced sharply, sometimes at or below cost as a **loss leader**, and the margin is recovered on the rest of the basket.
segments.tr: これらは厳しく価格設定され、時には**ロスリーダー**としてコストでまたはコスト以下で価格設定され、利益率は買い物かごの残りで回収されます。

segments.src: (Loss leaders are generally legal, though a number of states have minimum-markup laws, usually covering gas, alcohol, or tobacco.)
segments.tr: （ロスリーダーは一般的に法的ですが、多くの州には最低マークアップ法があり、通常ガス、アルコール、またはタバコをカバーしています。）

segments.src: And when inventory ages, **markdowns** are the release valve: a planned cadence of cuts that converts stale stock back into cash before it's worth nothing.
segments.tr: そして在庫が古くなるにつれて、**値下げ**がリリースバルブになります：陳腐化した在庫を何の価値もない状態になる前に現金に変換する計画的な値下げのサイクルです。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活での活用

segments.src: Sunday morning, a Kroger on the north side of Columbus.
segments.tr: 日曜の朝、コロンバス北部のクローガー。

segments.src: Your cart: a gallon of milk, cereal, toothpaste, tortilla chips, a rotisserie chicken.
segments.tr: あなたのカート：1ガロンの牛乳、シリアル、歯磨き粉、トルティーヤチップス、ロティサリーチキン。

segments.src: The milk is a key value item.
segments.tr: 牛乳は主要値引き商品です。

segments.src: It's priced within pennies of the Meijer two miles away because management assumes you know roughly what milk costs.
segments.tr: それは2マイル離れたマイヤーから数セント以内で価格設定されています。なぜなら、経営陣はあなたが牛乳の大体の価格を知っていると想定しているからです。

segments.src: The rotisserie chicken is close to a loss leader — cooked from a bird that would've been marked down anyway, priced to get you through the door on the one trip where you might also buy a $30 cut of steak.
segments.tr: ロティサリーチキンはほぼロスリーダーです—どうせ値下げされていただろう鶏から調理され、30ドルのステーキカットも購入する可能性のある1回の来店で店に招き入れるために価格設定されています。

segments.src: Costco has famously held its chicken at $4.99 for years for exactly this reason.
segments.tr: コストコは、正にこの理由で、チキンを数年間4.99ドルに固定してきたことで有名です。

segments.src: The toothpaste tells the category story.
segments.tr: 歯磨き粉はカテゴリーのストーリーを物語ります。

segments.src: Oral care is a routine category here, so you get maybe 40 SKUs, not 90, and the shelf runs a familiar pattern: a national brand at eye level, the Kroger store brand right beside it at a lower price and a higher margin, and the $9 whitening kit on the top shelf where it turns slowly but earns well when it does.
segments.tr: ここではオーラルケアはルーチン型カテゴリーであり、90ではなくおそらく40のSKUを得ます。そして棚は見慣れたパターンを実行します：目線の高さの全国ブランド、クローガーストアブランドがすぐ隣に低い価格と高い利益率で配置されています。そして、上の棚に9ドルのホワイトニングキットがあり、回転は遅いですが、売れるときは良く稼ぎます。

segments.src: The chips are near the front — high turns, decent margin, impulse-friendly placement.
segments.tr: チップスは前部付近にあります—高回転、適度な利益率、衝動買い向きの配置。

segments.src: And the endcap you walked past with the seasonal cooler display?
segments.tr: そして、季節型の冷蔵ディスプレイで通り過ぎたエンドキャップは？

segments.src: That's an occasional category, bought in a single seasonal buy, with a markdown schedule already written for late August.
segments.tr: それはたまに使うカテゴリーで、単一の季節購入で購入され、8月下旬のマークダウンスケジュールがすでに決められています。

segments.src: Nobody will scramble when it stops selling.
segments.tr: それが売れなくなるとき、誰も混乱することはありません。

segments.src: That was the plan in April.
segments.tr: それは4月の計画でした。

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 3行の要約

segments.src: 1. Category management treats each group of products as a business with an assigned role — destination, routine, occasional, or convenience — and that role drives assortment, space, and price aggressiveness.
segments.tr: 1. カテゴリー管理は、製品の各グループを、割り当てられた役割を持つビジネス—目的地、ルーチン、たまに、または利便—として扱い、その役割が品揃え、スペース、価格の積極性を左右します。

segments.src: 2. Inventory is capital, so retailers judge it by turns and GMROI (gross margin per dollar invested), balancing that against the cost of being out of stock.
segments.tr: 2. 在庫は資本であるため、小売業者はそれを回転率とGMROI（投資1ドルあたりの粗利益）で判定し、品切れのコストとバランスを取ります。

segments.src: 3. Pricing is a portfolio: sharp on the handful of key value items that shape price image, and recovered across everything else — under either an EDLP or a high–low strategy.
segments.tr: 3. 価格設定はポートフォリオです：価格イメージを形成する主要値引き商品の数に厳しく、その他すべてで回収されます—EDLPまたはハイロー戦略のいずれかの下で。

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 本日の用語

segments.src: - **Category management** — Managing a group of related products as a single business unit with its own role, strategy, and scorecard, rather than item by item.
segments.tr: - **カテゴリー管理**—関連製品のグループを、アイテムごとではなく、独自の役割、戦略、および成績表を持つ単一のビジネスユニットとして管理すること。

segments.src: - **Category role** — The job assigned to a category (destination, routine, occasional/seasonal, convenience), which determines its space, assortment breadth, and pricing posture.
segments.tr: - **カテゴリー役割**—カテゴリーに割り当てられた仕事（目的地、ルーチン、たまに/季節、利便）で、そのスペース、品揃え幅、および価格設定方針を決定するもの。

segments.src: - **GMROI** — Gross margin return on inventory investment: gross margin dollars divided by average inventory at cost; the profit earned per dollar tied up in stock.
segments.tr: - **GMROI**—在庫投資の粗利益リターン：粗利益ドルを原価での平均在庫で割った値；在庫に投入された1ドルあたりの稼ぎ。

segments.src: - **Inventory turnover** — How many times a year inventory is sold and replaced (COGS ÷ average inventory at cost); higher turns free up cash and reduce markdown risk.
segments.tr: - **在庫回転率**—1年間に在庫が販売・置き換えられる回数（売上原価÷原価での平均在庫）；高い回転は現金を解放し、マークダウンリスクを軽減します。

segments.src: - **EDLP vs. high–low** — Two pricing strategies: consistently low everyday prices, versus a higher base price punctuated by frequent deep promotions.
segments.tr: - **EDLPとハイロー戦略**—2つの価格設定戦略：一貫して低い毎日の価格対、頻繁な深いプロモーションで区切られたより高い基本価格。

de.title: [Einzelhandel 101 #9] Jede Warengruppe ist ein Geschäft – mit eigenem P&L

segments.src: > One-line summary: Advanced merchandising means running each category like a standalone business — giving it a job to do, measuring the return on the cash parked in its inventory, and setting prices that protect both margin and price image.
segments.tr: > Zusammenfassung in einem Satz: Fortgeschrittenes Merchandising bedeutet, jede Kategorie wie ein eigenständiges Geschäft zu betreiben – ihr eine Aufgabe zu geben, die Rendite des im Bestand gebundenen Kapitals zu messen und Preise festzulegen, die sowohl die Gewinnspanne als auch das Preisimage schützen.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Das heutige Konzept

segments.src: Last time we met the person who picked everything on the shelf six months before you walked in.
segments.tr: Beim letzten Mal haben wir die Person kennengelernt, die sechs Monate vor deinem Besuch alles ins Regal gestellt hat.

segments.src: Today: how they actually decide.
segments.tr: Heute: wie sie tatsächlich entscheiden.

segments.src: Three levers do most of the work.
segments.tr: Drei Hebel erledigen den Großteil der Arbeit.

segments.src: Category management — the aisle has a job.**
segments.tr: Kategorienmanagement – das Regal hat eine Aufgabe.**

segments.src: Instead of buying product by product, retailers group items the way shoppers think about them ("oral care," not "tubes we get from Colgate") and manage that group as a business unit.
segments.tr: Anstatt Produkt für Produkt zu kaufen, gruppieren Einzelhändler Artikel nach der Art, wie Käufer sie denken ("Zahnpflege" statt "Tuben von Colgate") und verwalten diese Gruppe als Geschäftseinheit.

segments.src: The framework, popularized in the 1990s through the industry's Efficient Consumer Response push, starts by assigning each category a **role**:
segments.tr: Das Rahmenwerk, das in den 1990er Jahren durch die Efficient Consumer Response Initiative der Branche populär gemacht wurde, beginnt damit, jeder Kategorie eine **Rolle** zuzuweisen:

segments.src: - **Destination** — a reason to choose this store over the one down the road. Deep assortment, sharp prices, lots of space.
segments.tr: - **Destination** — ein Grund, diesen Laden dem anderen vorzuziehen. Tiefes Sortiment, scharfe Preise, viel Platz.

segments.src: - **Routine** — the everyday workhorse that builds the basket and carries margin. Most of the store lives here.
segments.tr: - **Routine** – das alltägliche Arbeitstier, das den Warenkorb aufbaut und die Gewinnspanne trägt. Der Großteil des Ladens funktioniert damit.

segments.src: - **Occasional / seasonal** — grilling supplies in June, school glue in August.
segments.tr: - **Gelegentlich / saisonal** – Grillzubehör im Juni, Schulkleber im August.

segments.src: - **Convenience** — you didn't come for it, but it's there. Fewer options, healthier margins.
segments.tr: - **Convenience** – du bist nicht dafür gekommen, aber es ist da. Weniger Optionen, gesündere Margen.

segments.src: The role drives everything downstream: how many SKUs, how much shelf, how aggressive the price, how much promo money.
segments.tr: Die Rolle bestimmt alles Weitere: wie viele SKUs, wie viel Regalgrundfläche, wie aggressiv der Preis, wie viel Promogeld.

segments.src: A destination category and a convenience category get opposite treatment on purpose.
segments.tr: Eine Destinationskategorie und eine Convenience-Kategorie werden absichtlich gegensätzlich behandelt.

segments.src: One wrinkle worth knowing: retailers often name a **category captain** — usually the biggest supplier — to help build the plan, since that vendor has the best data.
segments.tr: Ein Punkt, den man kennen sollte: Einzelhändler ernennen oft einen **Kategorienleiter** – normalerweise der größte Lieferant – um den Plan zu entwickeln, da dieser Anbieter die besten Daten hat.

segments.src: It's efficient and it's a conflict of interest at the same time, which is why captains' recommendations get audited and why the practice draws antitrust attention.
segments.tr: Es ist effizient und gleichzeitig ein Interessenkonflikt, weshalb die Empfehlungen der Kategorienleiter überprüft werden und die Praxis kartellrechtliche Aufmerksamkeit erhält.

segments.src: Inventory management — the shelf is a bank account.**
segments.tr: Bestandsverwaltung – das Regal ist ein Bankkonto.**

segments.src: Every unit on that shelf is cash the retailer can't use for anything else.
segments.tr: Jede Einheit auf diesem Regal ist Bargeld, das der Einzelhändler nicht für etwas anderes verwenden kann.

segments.src: So the question isn't "did it sell?"
segments.tr: Die Frage ist also nicht "hat es sich verkauft?"

segments.src: but "what did it earn per dollar tied up?"
segments.tr: sondern "was hat es pro gebundenem Dollar verdient?"

segments.src: Two numbers carry the load:
segments.tr: Zwei Zahlen tragen die Last:

segments.src: inventory turnover = cost of goods sold / average inventory at cost
segments.tr: inventory turnover = cost of goods sold / average inventory at cost

segments.src: GMROI = gross margin dollars / average inventory at cost
segments.tr: GMROI = gross margin dollars / average inventory at cost

segments.src: weeks of supply = 52 / annual turns
segments.tr: weeks of supply = 52 / annual turns

segments.src: GMROI of 2.5 means the category returned $2.50 of gross margin for every $1 invested in inventory.
segments.tr: Ein GMROI von 2,5 bedeutet, dass die Kategorie 2,50 $ Bruttogewinnspanne pro $1 Bestandsinvestition zurückgab.

segments.src: This is why a low-margin item that turns 20 times a year can beat a high-margin item that turns twice — and why buyers argue about turns more than about markup.
segments.tr: Deshalb kann ein Artikel mit niedriger Gewinnspanne, der 20-mal pro Jahr umschlägt, einen Artikel mit hoher Gewinnspanne, der nur zweimal umschlägt, übertrumpfen – und deshalb diskutieren Käufer mehr über Umschläge als über Aufschläge.

segments.src: The counterweight is service level.
segments.tr: Das Gegengewicht ist das Serviceniveau.

segments.src: Order less and you free cash but risk an out-of-stock, which costs the sale and sometimes the trip.
segments.tr: Bestelle weniger und du befreist Bargeld, riskierst aber eine Fehlmenge, was den Verkauf und manchmal die Fahrt kostet.

segments.src: So teams hold **safety stock** and set a reorder point:
segments.tr: Teams halten also **Sicherheitsbestand** und setzen einen Bestellpunkt:

segments.src: reorder point = expected demand during lead time + safety stock
segments.tr: reorder point = expected demand during lead time + safety stock

segments.src: Then there's leakage.
segments.tr: Dann ist da noch der Schwund.

segments.src: **Shrink** — theft, damage, spoilage, paperwork errors — has run around 1.5% of sales in recent National Retail Federation security surveys.
segments.tr: **Schwund** – Diebstahl, Beschädigungen, Verderb, Buchhaltungsfehler – liegt in jüngsten Sicherheitsumfragen der National Retail Federation bei etwa 1,5 % des Umsatzes.

segments.src: On thin retail margins, that's not rounding.
segments.tr: Bei dünnen Einzelhandelsspannen ist das keine Rundung.

segments.src: Pricing — margin and image, at the same time.**
segments.tr: Preisgestaltung – Gewinnspanne und Image gleichzeitig.**

segments.src: The arithmetic is easy:
segments.tr: Die Rechnung ist einfach:

segments.src: retail price = cost / (1 - target margin %)
segments.tr: retail price = cost / (1 - target margin %)

segments.src: "Keystone" markup just means doubling cost: a $5 item retails at $10, a 50% margin.
segments.tr: "Keystone"-Aufschlag bedeutet nur die Verdopplung der Kosten: Ein Artikel für $5 wird für $10 im Einzelhandel verkauft, eine Gewinnspanne von 50 %.

segments.src: The strategy is the hard part, and it splits two ways.
segments.tr: Die Strategie ist der schwierige Teil, und er spaltet sich zwei Wege.

segments.src: **EDLP** (everyday low price) keeps prices flat and predictable — Walmart, Costco, Aldi.
segments.tr: **EDLP** (Everyday Low Price) hält die Preise flach und vorhersagbar – Walmart, Costco, Aldi.

segments.src: **High–low** runs a base price plus frequent, deep promotions, often gated behind a loyalty card — most conventional supermarkets and department stores.
segments.tr: **High-Low** läuft zu einem Basispreis plus häufigen, tiefgreifenden Promotionen, oft hinter einer Treuekarte – die meisten konventionellen Supermärkte und Kaufhäuser.

segments.src: EDLP smooths demand and cuts labor spent re-ticketing; high–low creates urgency and pulls in deal-sensitive shoppers, at the cost of training people to wait for the sale.
segments.tr: EDLP glättet die Nachfrage und senkt die Arbeit für das Neuauszeichnen; High-Low erzeugt Dringlichkeit und zieht preisgünstige Käufer an, auf Kosten der Schulung, auf den Ausverkauf zu warten.

segments.src: Either way, no one prices 40,000 items with equal care.
segments.tr: Egal wie, niemand bepreist 40.000 Artikel mit gleicher Sorgfalt.

segments.src: Shoppers only remember a few dozen **key value items** — milk, eggs, bananas, a 12-pack of soda — and those set the store's price image.
segments.tr: Käufer erinnern sich nur an ein Dutzend **Schlüsselwertartikel** – Milch, Eier, Bananen, ein 12er-Pack Limonade – und diese setzen das Preisimage des Ladens.

segments.src: Those get priced sharply, sometimes at or below cost as a **loss leader**, and the margin is recovered on the rest of the basket.
segments.tr: Diese werden scharf bepreist, manchmal zu oder unter den Kosten als **Lockvogel**, und die Gewinnspanne wird im Rest des Warenkorbs wieder hereingeholt.

segments.src: (Loss leaders are generally legal, though a number of states have minimum-markup laws, usually covering gas, alcohol, or tobacco.)
segments.tr: (Lockvögel sind im Allgemeinen legal, obwohl eine Reihe von Staaten Mindestaufschlagsgesetze haben, die normalerweise Benzin, Alkohol oder Tabak abdecken.)

segments.src: And when inventory ages, **markdowns** are the release valve: a planned cadence of cuts that converts stale stock back into cash before it's worth nothing.
segments.tr: Und wenn der Bestand altert, sind **Herabsetzungen** das Überdruckventil: ein geplanter Rhythmus von Senkungen, der veraltetes Lager vor Wertlosigkeit zurück in Bargeld umwandelt.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Im täglichen Leben

segments.src: Sunday morning, a Kroger on the north side of Columbus.
segments.tr: Sonntagmorgen, ein Kroger auf der Nordseite von Columbus.

segments.src: Your cart: a gallon of milk, cereal, toothpaste, tortilla chips, a rotisserie chicken.
segments.tr: Dein Warenkorb: eine Gallone Milch, Müsli, Zahnpasta, Tortilla-Chips, ein Rotisserie-Hähnchen.

segments.src: The milk is a key value item.
segments.tr: Die Milch ist ein Schlüsselwertartikel.

segments.src: It's priced within pennies of the Meijer two miles away because management assumes you know roughly what milk costs.
segments.tr: Sie wird um Centbeträge des Meijer zwei Meilen entfernt bepreist, weil das Management davon ausgeht, dass du grob weißt, wie viel Milch kostet.

segments.src: The rotisserie chicken is close to a loss leader — cooked from a bird that would've been marked down anyway, priced to get you through the door on the one trip where you might also buy a $30 cut of steak.
segments.tr: Das Rotisserie-Hähnchen ist fast ein Lockvogel – gekocht aus einem Vogel, der ohnehin herabgesetzt worden wäre, bepreist, um dich zur Tür herein auf der einen Fahrt zu bringen, auf der du möglicherweise auch ein $30-Steak kaufst.

segments.src: Costco has famously held its chicken at $4.99 for years for exactly this reason.
segments.tr: Costco hat sein Hähnchen für genau diesen Grund Jahre lang bei $4,99 gehalten.

segments.src: The toothpaste tells the category story.
segments.tr: Die Zahnpasta erzählt die Kategoriegeschichte.

segments.src: Oral care is a routine category here, so you get maybe 40 SKUs, not 90, and the shelf runs a familiar pattern: a national brand at eye level, the Kroger store brand right beside it at a lower price and a higher margin, and the $9 whitening kit on the top shelf where it turns slowly but earns well when it does.
segments.tr: Zahnpflege ist hier eine Routine-Kategorie, daher erhältst du etwa 40 SKUs statt 90, und das Regal folgt einem bekannten Muster: eine nationale Marke auf Augenhöhe, die Kroger-Eigenmarke daneben zu niedrigerem Preis und höherer Gewinnspanne, und ein $9-Aufhellungs-Kit oben, das sich langsam verkauft, aber gutes Geld verdient, wenn es verkauft wird.

segments.src: The chips are near the front — high turns, decent margin, impulse-friendly placement.
segments.tr: Die Chips sind vorne in der Nähe – hohe Umschläge, anständige Gewinnspanne, impulskäuferfreundliche Platzierung.

segments.src: And the endcap you walked past with the seasonal cooler display?
segments.tr: Und die Kopfzeile mit der saisonalen Kühldisplay, an der du vorbeigegangen bist?

segments.src: That's an occasional category, bought in a single seasonal buy, with a markdown schedule already written for late August.
segments.tr: Das ist eine Gelegenheitskategorie, die in einem einzigen saisonalen Kauf gekauft wird, mit einem bereits für Ende August vorgesehenen Herabsetzungsplan.

segments.src: Nobody will scramble when it stops selling.
segments.tr: Niemand wird durcheinander kommen, wenn es aufhört zu verkaufen.

segments.src: That was the plan in April.
segments.tr: Das war der Plan im April.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Zusammenfassung in drei Zeilen

segments.src: 1. Category management treats each group of products as a business with an assigned role — destination, routine, occasional, or convenience — and that role drives assortment, space, and price aggressiveness.
segments.tr: 1. Das Kategorienmanagement behandelt jede Produktgruppe als eigenständiges Geschäft mit zugewiesener Rolle – Destination, Routine, Gelegenheit oder Convenience – und diese Rolle bestimmt Sortiment, Platzangebot und Preisaggressivität.

segments.src: 2. Inventory is capital, so retailers judge it by turns and GMROI (gross margin per dollar invested), balancing that against the cost of being out of stock.
segments.tr: 2. Bestand ist Kapital, daher beurteilen Einzelhändler ihn nach Umschlägen und GMROI (Bruttogewinnspanne pro investiertem Dollar), das gegen die Kosten für Fehlmengen abgewogen wird.

segments.src: 3. Pricing is a portfolio: sharp on the handful of key value items that shape price image, and recovered across everything else — under either an EDLP or a high–low strategy.
segments.tr: 3. Preisgestaltung ist ein Portfolio: scharf bei der Handvoll Schlüsselwertartikel, die das Preisimage prägen, und wieder hereingeholt über alles andere – unter entweder einer EDLP- oder einer High-Low-Strategie.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Heutige Begriffe

segments.src: - **Category management** — Managing a group of related products as a single business unit with its own role, strategy, and scorecard, rather than item by item.
segments.tr: - **Kategorienmanagement** – Verwaltung einer Gruppe verwandter Produkte als einzelne Geschäftseinheit mit eigener Rolle, Strategie und Leistungsanzeige, nicht von Artikel zu Artikel.

segments.src: - **Category role** — The job assigned to a category (destination, routine, occasional/seasonal, convenience), which determines its space, assortment breadth, and pricing posture.
segments.tr: - **Kategorienrolle** – Die einer Kategorie zugewiesene Aufgabe (Destination, Routine, Gelegenheit/saisonal, Convenience), die deren Platzangebot, Sortimentsbreite und Preisposition bestimmt.

segments.src: - **GMROI** — Gross margin return on inventory investment: gross margin dollars divided by average inventory at cost; the profit earned per dollar tied up in stock.
segments.tr: - **GMROI** – Rentabilität der Bestandsinvestition: Bruttogewinnspanne in Dollar geteilt durch durchschnittliche Bestandskosten; der pro Dollar Bestandsinvestition verdiente Gewinn.

segments.src: - **Inventory turnover** — How many times a year inventory is sold and replaced (COGS ÷ average inventory at cost); higher turns free up cash and reduce markdown risk.
segments.tr: - **Bestandsumschlag** – Wie oft pro Jahr der Bestand verkauft und ersetzt wird (COGS ÷ durchschnittliche Bestandskosten); höhere Umschläge geben Kapital frei und senken das Herabsetzungsrisiko.

segments.src: - **EDLP vs. high–low** — Two pricing strategies: consistently low everyday prices, versus a higher base price punctuated by frequent deep promotions.
segments.tr: - **EDLP vs. High-Low** – Zwei Preisstrategien: Durchgehend niedrige Alltagspreise gegenüber einem höheren Basispreis mit häufigen Tiefpreisaktionen.

vi.title: [Bán lẻ 101 #9] Mỗi Lối Đi Là Một Doanh Nghiệp Nhỏ, và Nó Có P&L Riêng của Nó

segments.src: > One-line summary: Advanced merchandising means running each category like a standalone business — giving it a job to do, measuring the return on the cash parked in its inventory, and setting prices that protect both margin and price image.
segments.tr: > Tóm tắt một dòng: Hàng hóa nâng cao có nghĩa là điều hành từng danh mục như một doanh nghiệp độc lập — giao cho nó một công việc cần làm, đo lường lợi suất từ tiền mặt nằm trong kho hàng của nó, và đặt giá để bảo vệ cả lợi nhuận gộp lẫn hình ảnh giá cả.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Khái Niệm Hôm Nay

segments.src: Last time we met the person who picked everything on the shelf six months before you walked in.
segments.tr: Lần cuối cùng chúng ta gặp người đã chọn mọi thứ trên kệ sáu tháng trước khi bạn bước vào.

segments.src: Today: how they actually decide.
segments.tr: Hôm nay: làm thế nào họ thực sự quyết định.

segments.src: Three levers do most of the work.
segments.tr: Ba đòn bẩy thực hiện hầu hết công việc.

segments.src: Category management — the aisle has a job.**
segments.tr: Quản lý danh mục — lối đi có một công việc.**

segments.src: Instead of buying product by product, retailers group items the way shoppers think about them ("oral care," not "tubes we get from Colgate") and manage that group as a business unit.
segments.tr: Thay vì mua sản phẩm từng cái một, các nhà bán lẻ nhóm các mặt hàng theo cách mà người mua sắm suy nghĩ về chúng ("chăm sóc miệng," không phải "các ống chúng ta nhận từ Colgate") và quản lý nhóm đó như một đơn vị kinh doanh.

segments.src: The framework, popularized in the 1990s through the industry's Efficient Consumer Response push, starts by assigning each category a **role**:
segments.tr: Khuôn khổ, được phổ biến vào những năm 1990 thông qua nỗ lực Phản ứng Hiệu quả cho Người tiêu dùng của ngành, bắt đầu bằng cách gán cho mỗi danh mục một **vai trò**:

segments.src: - **Destination** — a reason to choose this store over the one down the road. Deep assortment, sharp prices, lots of space.
segments.tr: - **Điểm đến** — lý do để chọn cửa hàng này hơn cửa hàng ở phía kia. Phân loại sâu, giá cạnh tranh, nhiều không gian.

segments.src: - **Routine** — the everyday workhorse that builds the basket and carries margin. Most of the store lives here.
segments.tr: - **Thường lệ** — mặt hàng hàng ngày là nền tảng giỏ hàng và tạo lợi nhuận. Hầu hết cửa hàng ở đây.

segments.src: - **Occasional / seasonal** — grilling supplies in June, school glue in August.
segments.tr: - **Theo mùa / Đặc biệt** — dụng cụ nướng lạp xưởng vào tháng 6, keo trường học vào tháng 8.

segments.src: - **Convenience** — you didn't come for it, but it's there. Fewer options, healthier margins.
segments.tr: - **Tiện lợi** — bạn không đến vì nó, nhưng nó ở đó. Lựa chọn ít hơn, lợi nhuận cao hơn.

segments.src: The role drives everything downstream: how many SKUs, how much shelf, how aggressive the price, how much promo money.
segments.tr: Vai trò này quyết định mọi thứ phía sau: có bao nhiêu SKU, bao nhiêu không gian kệ, giá bao nhiêu tích cực, bao nhiêu tiền khuyến mãi.

segments.src: A destination category and a convenience category get opposite treatment on purpose.
segments.tr: Một danh mục điểm đến và một danh mục tiện lợi nhận được xử lý trái ngược một cách có chủ đích.

segments.src: One wrinkle worth knowing: retailers often name a **category captain** — usually the biggest supplier — to help build the plan, since that vendor has the best data.
segments.tr: Một chi tiết đáng lưu ý: các nhà bán lẻ thường gọi một **thủ lĩnh danh mục** — thường là nhà cung cấp lớn nhất — để giúp xây dựng kế hoạch, vì nhà cung cấp đó có dữ liệu tốt nhất.

segments.src: It's efficient and it's a conflict of interest at the same time, which is why captains' recommendations get audited and why the practice draws antitrust attention.
segments.tr: Nó hiệu quả và đồng thời cũng là xung đột lợi ích, đó là lý do tại sao các khuyến nghị của thủ lĩnh được kiểm toán và tại sao thực hành này thu hút sự chú ý chống độc quyền.

segments.src: Inventory management — the shelf is a bank account.**
segments.tr: Quản lý hàng tồn kho — kệ là tài khoản ngân hàng.**

segments.src: Every unit on that shelf is cash the retailer can't use for anything else.
segments.tr: Mỗi đơn vị trên kệ đó là tiền mặt mà nhà bán lẻ không thể sử dụng cho bất cứ điều gì khác.

segments.src: So the question isn't "did it sell?"
segments.tr: Vì vậy, câu hỏi không phải là "nó đã bán được không?"

segments.src: but "what did it earn per dollar tied up?"
segments.tr: mà là "nó kiếm được bao nhiêu trên mỗi đô la bị buộc?"

segments.src: Two numbers carry the load:
segments.tr: Hai con số mang lại gánh nặng:

segments.src: inventory turnover = cost of goods sold / average inventory at cost
segments.tr: inventory turnover = cost of goods sold / average inventory at cost

segments.src: GMROI = gross margin dollars / average inventory at cost
segments.tr: GMROI = gross margin dollars / average inventory at cost

segments.src: weeks of supply = 52 / annual turns
segments.tr: weeks of supply = 52 / annual turns

segments.src: GMROI of 2.5 means the category returned $2.50 of gross margin for every $1 invested in inventory.
segments.tr: GMROI 2,5 có nghĩa là danh mục trả về $2,50 lợi nhuận gộp cho mỗi $1 đầu tư vào hàng tồn kho.

segments.src: This is why a low-margin item that turns 20 times a year can beat a high-margin item that turns twice — and why buyers argue about turns more than about markup.
segments.tr: Đây là lý do tại sao một mặt hàng lợi nhuận thấp quay vòng 20 lần một năm có thể đánh bại một mặt hàng lợi nhuận cao quay vòng hai lần — và tại sao người mua thường tranh luận về vòng quay nhiều hơn so với mức giá.

segments.src: The counterweight is service level.
segments.tr: Cân bằng đối trọng là mức độ dịch vụ.

segments.src: Order less and you free cash but risk an out-of-stock, which costs the sale and sometimes the trip.
segments.tr: Đặt hàng ít hơn và bạn giải phóng tiền mặt nhưng rủi ro hết hàng, điều này chi phí cho bán hàng và đôi khi cả chuyến đi.

segments.src: So teams hold **safety stock** and set a reorder point:
segments.tr: Vì vậy các đội giữ **dự trữ an toàn** và đặt điểm đặt hàng lại:

segments.src: reorder point = expected demand during lead time + safety stock
segments.tr: reorder point = expected demand during lead time + safety stock

segments.src: Then there's leakage.
segments.tr: Rồi có rò rỉ.

segments.src: **Shrink** — theft, damage, spoilage, paperwork errors — has run around 1.5% of sales in recent National Retail Federation security surveys.
segments.tr: **Mất hàng** — ăn cắp, hỏng hóc, hư hỏng, lỗi giấy tờ — đã chạy khoảng 1,5% bán hàng trong các cuộc khảo sát an niều gần đây của Liên đoàn Bán lẻ Quốc gia.

segments.src: On thin retail margins, that's not rounding.
segments.tr: Trên lợi nhuận bán lẻ mỏng, đó không phải là làm tròn.

segments.src: Pricing — margin and image, at the same time.**
segments.tr: Định giá — lợi nhuận và hình ảnh, cùng lúc.**

segments.src: The arithmetic is easy:
segments.tr: Số học là đơn giản:

segments.src: retail price = cost / (1 - target margin %)
segments.tr: retail price = cost / (1 - target margin %)

segments.src: "Keystone" markup just means doubling cost: a $5 item retails at $10, a 50% margin.
segments.tr: "Keystone" đánh dấu chỉ có nghĩa là chi phí tăng gấp đôi: một mặt hàng $5 bán lẻ ở $10, lợi nhuận 50%.

segments.src: The strategy is the hard part, and it splits two ways.
segments.tr: Chiến lược là phần khó, và nó tách thành hai cách.

segments.src: **EDLP** (everyday low price) keeps prices flat and predictable — Walmart, Costco, Aldi.
segments.tr: **EDLP** (giá thấp hàng ngày) giữ giá cố định và có thể dự đoán được — Walmart, Costco, Aldi.

segments.src: **High–low** runs a base price plus frequent, deep promotions, often gated behind a loyalty card — most conventional supermarkets and department stores.
segments.tr: **Cao-thấp** chạy một giá cơ sở cộng với các khuyến mãi sâu thường xuyên, thường bị giới hạn sau thẻ trung thành — hầu hết các siêu thị thông thường và cửa hàng bộ phận.

segments.src: EDLP smooths demand and cuts labor spent re-ticketing; high–low creates urgency and pulls in deal-sensitive shoppers, at the cost of training people to wait for the sale.
segments.tr: EDLP làm mịn nhu cầu và giảm lao động dành cho việc dán nhãn lại; cao-thấp tạo ra tính cấp bách và kéo vào những người mua nhạy cảm với thương vụ, với chi phí đào tạo mọi người chờ đợi bán hàng.

segments.src: Either way, no one prices 40,000 items with equal care.
segments.tr: Dù bằng cách nào, không ai định giá 40.000 mặt hàng với sự chăm sóc bằng nhau.

segments.src: Shoppers only remember a few dozen **key value items** — milk, eggs, bananas, a 12-pack of soda — and those set the store's price image.
segments.tr: Người mua sắm chỉ nhớ một vài chục **mặt hàng giá trị chính** — sữa, trứng, chuối, một gói 12 lon soda — và những cái này thiết lập hình ảnh giá của cửa hàng.

segments.src: Those get priced sharply, sometimes at or below cost as a **loss leader**, and the margin is recovered on the rest of the basket.
segments.tr: Những cái này được định giá cạnh tranh, đôi khi ở hoặc dưới giá vốn như một **hàng bán lỗ**, và lợi nhuận được khôi phục trên phần còn lại của giỏ hàng.

segments.src: (Loss leaders are generally legal, though a number of states have minimum-markup laws, usually covering gas, alcohol, or tobacco.)
segments.tr: (Hàng bán lỗ thường hợp pháp, mặc dù một số bang có luật đánh dấu tối thiểu, thường bao gồm xăng, rượu hoặc thuốc lá.)

segments.src: And when inventory ages, **markdowns** are the release valve: a planned cadence of cuts that converts stale stock back into cash before it's worth nothing.
segments.tr: Và khi hàng tồn kho lão hóa, **hạ giá** là van xả: một lịch trình được lên kế hoạch của những khoản cắt chuyển đổi cổ phiếu cũ thành tiền mặt trước khi nó không còn giá trị gì.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Trong Cuộc Sống Hàng Ngày

segments.src: Sunday morning, a Kroger on the north side of Columbus.
segments.tr: Sáng chủ nhật, một Kroger ở phía bắc Columbus.

segments.src: Your cart: a gallon of milk, cereal, toothpaste, tortilla chips, a rotisserie chicken.
segments.tr: Giỏ hàng của bạn: một gallon sữa, ngũ cốc, kem đánh răng, bánh tortilla chips, một con gà quay.

segments.src: The milk is a key value item.
segments.tr: Sữa là một mặt hàng giá trị chính.

segments.src: It's priced within pennies of the Meijer two miles away because management assumes you know roughly what milk costs.
segments.tr: Nó được định giá trong vài xu của Meijer hai dặm xa vì quản lý giả định bạn biết xấp xỉ sữa giá bao nhiêu.

segments.src: The rotisserie chicken is close to a loss leader — cooked from a bird that would've been marked down anyway, priced to get you through the door on the one trip where you might also buy a $30 cut of steak.
segments.tr: Con gà quay gần như là một hàng bán lỗ — nấu từ một con chim đã bị hạ giá, được định giá để dẫn bạn vào cửa hàng trong chuyến duy nhất nơi bạn cũng có thể mua một miếng thịt $30.

segments.src: Costco has famously held its chicken at $4.99 for years for exactly this reason.
segments.tr: Costco nổi tiếng đã giữ con gà của nó ở $4,99 trong nhiều năm chính vì lý do này.

segments.src: The toothpaste tells the category story.
segments.tr: Kem đánh răng kể về câu chuyện danh mục.

segments.src: Oral care is a routine category here, so you get maybe 40 SKUs, not 90, and the shelf runs a familiar pattern: a national brand at eye level, the Kroger store brand right beside it at a lower price and a higher margin, and the $9 whitening kit on the top shelf where it turns slowly but earns well when it does.
segments.tr: Chăm sóc miệng là một danh mục thường lệ ở đây, vì vậy bạn nhận được khoảng 40 SKU thay vì 90, và kệ tuân theo một mô hình quen thuộc: một thương hiệu quốc gia ở mức mắt, thương hiệu cửa hàng Kroger ngay bên cạnh với giá thấp hơn và lợi nhuận cao hơn, và bộ dụng cụ làm trắng $9 trên kệ trên cùng nơi nó quay vòng chậm nhưng sinh lợi tốt.

segments.src: The chips are near the front — high turns, decent margin, impulse-friendly placement.
segments.tr: Các chip gần phía trước — vòng quay cao, lợi nhuận tốt, vị trí thân thiện với động cơ.

segments.src: And the endcap you walked past with the seasonal cooler display?
segments.tr: Và endcap bạn đã đi qua với hiển thị cooler theo mùa?

segments.src: That's an occasional category, bought in a single seasonal buy, with a markdown schedule already written for late August.
segments.tr: Đó là một danh mục theo mùa, được mua trong một lần mua hàng theo mùa duy nhất, với lịch trình hạ giá đã được viết cho cuối tháng 8.

segments.src: Nobody will scramble when it stops selling.
segments.tr: Sẽ không ai vật lộn khi nó ngừng bán.

segments.src: That was the plan in April.
segments.tr: Đó là kế hoạch vào tháng 4.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Bản Tóm Tắt Ba Dòng

segments.src: 1. Category management treats each group of products as a business with an assigned role — destination, routine, occasional, or convenience — and that role drives assortment, space, and price aggressiveness.
segments.tr: 1. Quản lý danh mục coi mỗi nhóm sản phẩm là một doanh nghiệp có vai trò được gán — điểm đến, thường lệ, theo mùa hoặc tiện lợi — và vai trò đó quyết định phân loại, không gian và chiến lược giá.

segments.src: 2. Inventory is capital, so retailers judge it by turns and GMROI (gross margin per dollar invested), balancing that against the cost of being out of stock.
segments.tr: 2. Hàng tồn kho là vốn, vì vậy các nhà bán lẻ đánh giá nó bằng vòng quay và GMROI (lợi nhuận gộp trên mỗi đô la đầu tư), cân bằng điều này chống lại chi phí hết hàng.

segments.src: 3. Pricing is a portfolio: sharp on the handful of key value items that shape price image, and recovered across everything else — under either an EDLP or a high–low strategy.
segments.tr: 3. Định giá là một danh mục đầu tư: cạnh tranh trên một số mặt hàng giá trị chính hình thành hình ảnh giá, và khôi phục trên phần còn lại — dưới chiến lược EDLP hoặc cao-thấp.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Các Điều Khoản Hôm Nay

segments.src: - **Category management** — Managing a group of related products as a single business unit with its own role, strategy, and scorecard, rather than item by item.
segments.tr: - **Quản lý danh mục** — Quản lý một nhóm sản phẩm liên quan như một đơn vị kinh doanh duy nhất với vai trò, chiến lược và bảng điểm riêng của nó, thay vì từng mặt hàng một.

segments.src: - **Category role** — The job assigned to a category (destination, routine, occasional/seasonal, convenience), which determines its space, assortment breadth, and pricing posture.
segments.tr: - **Vai trò danh mục** — Công việc được gán cho một danh mục (điểm đến, thường lệ, theo mùa / đặc biệt, tiện lợi), xác định không gian, độ rộng phân loại và lập trường giá của nó.

segments.src: - **GMROI** — Gross margin return on inventory investment: gross margin dollars divided by average inventory at cost; the profit earned per dollar tied up in stock.
segments.tr: - **GMROI** — Lợi nhuận gộp trên đầu tư hàng tồn kho: đô la lợi nhuận gộp chia cho hàng tồn kho trung bình ở giá vốn; lợi nhuận kiếm được trên mỗi đô la bị buộc trong cổ phiếu.

segments.src: - **Inventory turnover** — How many times a year inventory is sold and replaced (COGS ÷ average inventory at cost); higher turns free up cash and reduce markdown risk.
segments.tr: - **Vòng quay hàng tồn kho** — Bao nhiêu lần một năm hàng tồn kho được bán và thay thế (COGS ÷ hàng tồn kho trung bình ở giá vốn); vòng quay cao hơn giải phóng tiền mặt và giảm rủi ro hạ giá.

segments.src: - **EDLP vs. high–low** — Two pricing strategies: consistently low everyday prices, versus a higher base price punctuated by frequent deep promotions.
segments.tr: - **EDLP so với cao-thấp** — Hai chiến lược định giá: giá thấp ổn định hàng ngày, so với giá cơ sở cao hơn được ngắt quãng bằng các khuyến mãi sâu thường xuyên.
